body_fields.quote: the hold bounds the driver, never the human: any human key still hands the held dialog back at once, whatever the hold. A `viola send` on a verified CLI waits in the readiness gate for the input box for at most `GATE_MAX_WAIT` (8.5 s, architecture [Screen Model]) and is then refused `not-delivered` / `input-not-ready` with nothing typed. That bound falls on the driver only as well: a key pressed during the wait goes to the child and takes the wheel at once, and the waiting send is then refused `human-typing`.

every time bound viola holds — the `viola wait` timeout the caller passes, the MCP `wait` cap, the dialog hold, the `viola send` readiness gate, the confirmation windows, the status-line deadline, the `claude agents --json` read, the budget pause — falls on the driver, the user's own command or viola's own child, never on the human: no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it.

body_fields.why: The refusal layout, typed exit codes, hint-free --json and the Unix-only socket-directory and revive --json refusals must read the same on all three OS legs.
body_fields.quote: **CLI:** `unable  <reason>  <detail>` on stderr, then `hint:` as the last stderr line, with a typed exit code. The one refusal with no hint is `unknown` (exit 14): its detail is a code word or nothing, opaque to a reader, so design prints no hint rather than a guess. Faults (`error: wrapper fault`, `error: internal error`) are not refusals and carry no hint. `--json` gives one document with no hint, except the `viola answer` and `viola send` exit-2 paths (below). Without `--json`, the exit-1 refusals of `viola revive`, and `viola run`'s socket-directory refusal (`refuse_socket_dir`, on the start both verbs share), take the fixed-message form of design-system cli pattern 2 (one `unable: <text>` line, then one `hint:` line last; a clap usage error exits 2), pinned by the root cases in `tests/cli_revive.rs` and, for the socket-directory refusal, by `a_loosened_socket_directory_on_a_start_is_socket_dir_refused` in `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`; under `--json` every refusal of the start `revive` shares with `run` gives one `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` document with no hint and empty stderr (`revive_json_*` in `tests/cli_revive.rs`, the start rows in `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`; chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract).

trycmd pins the `unable <reason> <detail>` + final `hint:` layout per refusal and assert_cmd the typed exit codes and a hint-free `--json`, on all three OS legs (the frame verbs' server-verify peer pid witness on windows-2025 and ubuntu-latest only: macOS reports no peer pid, the word there an euid mismatch alone; the socket-directory refusal on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest).
NEVER show error without recovery suggestion (per SC 3.3.3). Every human-mode CLI refusal except `unknown` (exit 14, its detail a code word or nothing, design cli) ends with a `hint:` line.
Every kebab-case reason/detail code (`not-delivered`, `human-typing`, `unverified-cli`) always sits beside the plain word `unable`.

body_fields.quote: **CLI, a name with no endpoint:** the refusal reads the instance directory: a directory is `instance-dead`, anything else (absent, a regular file, a symlink) is `unwrapped-name`, and the strict-modes check stays first.

body:
Brings `viola run` on Linux and macOS onto portable-pty's openpty backend behind the same pty seam as Windows' ConPTY: spawn, read, write, resize, wait and kill behave as the Windows wrapper's do, as far as the fake agent can read them.
Makes the full fake-agent suite the same on all three OSes: every end-to-end and integration test of a behaviour the two Unix OSes share runs on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest, and each test left cfg(windows), cfg(unix) or cfg(target_os) names the reason its behaviour belongs to one OS.
Re-reads the obs gates G1 to G4 and the CI test, perf and lint jobs, which must be green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest beside windows-2025, and keeps one diagnostics schema on every OS (process-log lines, events.ndjson, snapshots, every --json document).
Takes up the carried integration-tier witness of dim only on stale rows (v1-40) under the outer PTY. It also carries the wrapper-kill read on Unix and the reply-probe hypothesis, all on the fake agent with no live claude session; Windows behaviour, pins and tests do not move.

body_fields.what: the test, perf and lint jobs over matrix.os reading green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest beside windows-2025

body: The cli surface's output discipline, run on the ubuntu-latest and macos-latest legs: no SGR, glyph or cursor control of viola's own under non-TTY, NO_COLOR, TERM=dumb, --json, viola run or a passed viola revive; every SGR span beside its word; C0/C1 control characters escaped except \n and \t, which list rows escape too.

The tui passthrough boundary under the openpty wrapper (path P4): viola writes zero terminal bytes except the child's output, human keystrokes go through unblocked past the current atomic paste, and focus, mouse and resize sequences and terminal replies do not count as human editing and do not move the wheel on Linux and macOS. On windows-2025 the platform fact stays that an injected mouse report takes the wheel (F-W3).
The boundary after a contained vt100 feed panic: no viola literal on the outer terminal on every OS, and the child's own bytes on Unix.

Visual SGR values the outer-PTY witness of dim only on stale rows reads: dim SGR on stale rows only, bold only on NAME values, amber only on the DIALOG word, each state still carried by its word, unable and fail never coloured. The plan's Owed line under ARIA Patterns & Roles assigns this witness to the Linux and macOS parity entry.

Unwrapped NAME truncation under the outer PTY: cut with ... only on a terminal too narrow, never inside a \xHH escape; a wrapped NAME, piped output and --json are never cut. This applies when resize behaves under openpty as it does under ConPTY.

Path P6 board, wait/last and verify output on the Unix legs: linear static output, waiting: <name> once on stderr and on a TTY only, verify step lines [NN/NN] … pass|fail, the CAPTION literal order NAME · LIVE · STATUS · WHEEL · DIALOG · CLI, and the -- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY -- separator only when unwrapped rows exist.

Error recovery layout on all three OS legs: unable <reason> <detail> on stderr then hint: as the last stderr line, typed exit codes, and hint-free --json. The exceptions are unknown (exit 14, no hint) and the answer and send exit-2 fixed stderr line with no document. Diagnostics must carry the same words on every OS.

The per-OS split the error-recovery verification names: the frame verbs' server-verify peer pid witness runs on windows-2025 and ubuntu-latest only. On macOS there is no peer pid, so the word is an euid mismatch alone and no test reads it as a pid or start-time comparison (the recorded macOS carve-out). The socket-directory refusal (one unable: <text> line) runs on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest.

viola revive --json on the Unix legs: every refusal of the start it shares with run prints one exit-1 document (batch-script-child, pinned-hash-mismatch, squatted-name, program-not-found internal-error), and a pump_child error prints none, because the child has held the terminal.

Fixed CLI strings stay identical on every OS: they are pinned by trycmd or, for viola list, --help, plugin install, the server-verify, socket-directory, unwrapped-name and endpoint-lost hints and the link/unlink result lines, by literal. Any OS-only wording fails these pins.

Every time bound the Unix wrapper holds (send readiness gate, confirmation windows, dialog hold, status-line deadline, the wait timeout and cap, the budget pause) falls on the driver, the user's command or viola's own child, never on the human: no key is blocked, refused or delayed by it.

Where the cli and tui cases run and land: inside nextest-integration / nextest-e2e locally and, in CI, inside each per-OS test job's single instrumented coverage suite. Each leg's gate --require coverage,doctest is its own verdict and never allows skips; failures land in the run JSON's suites[].failures[]. A breach (suite-failed, suite-skipped, suite-missing, artifact-missing) fails the build.
The fake-agent Unix suite reads only viola's own bytes and the boundary. It never parses the rendered claude TUI screen for content and never takes screenshots as a11y evidence (R7).

body_fields.convention: each new cli output-discipline or tui boundary test runs inside the existing nextest-integration / nextest-e2e suites (CI: the per-OS coverage suite) on all three OS legs; no new suite enum value such as a11y without a Decisions Log entry, and no separate a11y driver outside scripts/agent-run.* run
each new test obeys zero flakiness: retries 0, no retry-once policy for a11y violations, #[ignore] banned, a flake keeps the chunk red until the root cause is fixed
no new cli or tui test result is cited as WCAG conformance evidence; assert_cmd / trycmd / portable-pty results are output-discipline stand-ins for SC 1.3.2, 1.4.1 and 3.3.1 only
no new a11y artifact upload and no stage or performance budget of its own; a cli or tui failure is a nextest failure in the harness run JSON
an output-discipline invariant that lives in crate tests falls under the epoch-boundary mutation audit (run --mutants)

body: The frontend's keyboard navigation, screen-reader and visual-design rules for 0.2.0: the frontend stays deferred and its technology is unchosen.

The Claude Code plugin entity (hooks, hook statusline, stdio MCP server) and the wrapper IPC channel: they are not-assertable machine-to-machine traffic with no UI surface, and hook keeps its contract.
The internal crates entity: it is library-only and not assertable.
The manual screen-reader passes (NVDA, VoiceOver, Orca) and the manual keyboard pass on P4 and P6: they are founder-owned supplements, and this chunk runs no live session and no attended pass.
The tui screen-reader row for Windows (NVDA + Windows Terminal, the O1 step) and the Windows ConPTY byte reading owed to Windows-only live measurements: no Windows behaviour moves in this chunk.
The compliance cross-check and the not-triggered wcag-mapping and regulated-compliance triggers: no regime applies to any surface.
The not-triggered target-size and multi-language triggers: there is no touch surface and no i18n convention, and Cyrillic, emoji and CJK appear only as passthrough content.
Plain-language reading level: SC 3.1.5 is not claimed and no readability scorer is introduced (D-A11Y-16).
The A11y Decisions Log history and its amendments archive: they are history, not a rule over this change.
The a11y tier justification and the POUR signal pyramid in their own right: they summarise the strategy and set no requirement beyond the surfaces and paths named in the needs.

body: **2026-09-24-supply-chain-and-workflow-gates** (Platform: ci.yml is the one push/PR workflow) — §9 Platform reads "one push/PR workflow `ci.yml`"; `nightly.yml` carries no a11y step. Any Unix a11y/boundary case this chunk adds or ungates runs in `ci.yml`'s three-OS matrix, never in nightly.

**2026-09-24-quality-gates** (CLI output-discipline evidence under the CI `coverage` suite) — the CLI output-discipline tests run on all three OS legs and in CI report inside the per-OS `test` job's single `coverage` suite under `gate --require coverage,doctest`. Origin of the §9 binding: Unix parity cases join that suite, not a new one.

**2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows** (Windows zero-viola-bytes oracle is literal absence) — split the zero-viola-bytes clause: viola's literals absent on every leg; byte-for-byte against an unwrapped run holds on Linux and macOS only (ConPTY emits its own preamble). §6 became "zero SGR of viola's own". This chunk's openpty wrapper is where the full byte-for-byte oracle must actually hold; the Windows literal-absence oracle must not move.

**2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary** — the CLI output-discipline invariants (P4, P6) in crate tests meet mutation only at the epoch-boundary `run --mutants` audit. Context for the stale-dim CARRY: it was held at the unit tier because the `mutants` profile's 10 s kill left no room beside the 5 s stale threshold; an outer-PTY witness here must stay workable under that profile.

**2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty** (the Windows zero-viola-bytes check names both ConPTY hosts) — Windows check (viola's literals absent) runs on both the sideloaded `OpenConsole.exe` and the inbox fallback; §6 credits both hosts' SGR/cursor/query bytes. Windows stays the live-supported target: no Unix case may move this oracle.

**2026-09-29-t15-07-57-wrap** (registry migration U35) — lifted into §3 tool pick: the tests' portable-pty `=0.8.1` pin is an inherited risk (0.9.0 maintained) that a11y never re-pins (D-A11Y-13). The openpty backend and the outer-PTY driver both sit on that crate; a re-pin is not a11y's to make.

**2026-10-04-the-wheel** (terminal replies non-editing, the Windows platform fact) — non-editing set became the closed list (focus, mouse X10/SGR/urxvt, replies DA1, DA2, CPR, DECRPM, kitty flags, OSC, DCS); case (3) landed step-wise (resize behind its size receipt, focus with a mouse read barrier, wheel probed by an `answer`, exit 13 driver / 10 human), full assertion on Linux and macOS, F-W3 platform fact on windows-2025. body: **Stack PTY layer ↔ Established Decisions [PTY]**: the openpty backend on Linux and macOS must keep the seam's contract the decision states: child exit detected on the process handle, never on EOF, no human key held behind a resize and DA1 never answered by viola, with portable-pty staying `=0.8.1` (architecture/stack-and-technologies fct-kxiazeyf) (architecture fct-omwrdnlc).

**Stack concurrency row ↔ Cross-cutting Tokio containment**: new code on the `run` or pty path uses std threads and blocking I/O, `viola-pty` staying a sync crate under the sole-root `cargo deny` tokio ban (architecture/stack-and-technologies fct-7z3oulbd) (architecture fct-me2myqzf) (architecture fct-l5jpezvw).

**Stack Wrapper IPC rows ↔ Occupied Resources Linux / macOS endpoint and the Instance snapshot**: the parity suite reads the 0700 socket dir, chmod 0600 and the owning-euid admission on both Unix OSes, and the pid and `started_at` server check on Linux only, macOS keeping its recorded no-peer-pid gap (architecture/stack-and-technologies fct-q5vugilx) (architecture/stack-and-technologies fct-vp2lxvsd) (architecture fct-wular7qm) (architecture fct-ld365mzq).

**Stack process liveness ↔ Standard Contracts Session liveness**: the v1-40 witness's stale wrapper is a heartbeat older than 5 s, and the kill-and-revive case reads the child gone by pid plus start time (architecture/stack-and-technologies fct-cnnrnbfw) (architecture fct-arftgre4).

**Stack logging and versioning rows ↔ Occupied Resources diagnostics and schemas, Data model optional fields**: the process-log lines conform to `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` on every OS, codes only in the role files, and a field one OS cannot fill is omitted or null, never an OS-only word (architecture/stack-and-technologies fct-rzlme45f) (architecture/stack-and-technologies fct-zse22tqm) (architecture fct-5jecrew3) (architecture fct-gn6wx4l2) (architecture fct-u5xw5irn).

**Design Philosophy ↔ Cross-cutting cross-platform discipline**: every OS-specific branch the chunk leaves or adds compiles and is tested on its CI runner, nothing shells out but `hook statusline`, children spawned directly, and no Windows behaviour, pin or test moves to make a Unix case pass (architecture fct-igbvtfv6) (architecture fct-fa2klbw5).

body_fields.why: the Linux and macOS wrapper must run its child through this same pinned seam, its exit read on the process handle, so spawn, read, write, resize, wait and kill behave as the Windows wrapper's do.
body_fields.quote: **[PTY] portable-pty `=0.8.1` pinned behind viola's own `pty` seam (spawn · read · write · resize · wait · kill).** Child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF, because ConPTY does not close the output stream on exit. If 0.8.1's Windows `kill()` misbehaves, the fallback is `TerminateProcess` on `child.process_id()` via windows-sys.

Child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF; on Windows x64 the ConPTY is sideloaded, failing open to the inbox one, and every `viola` process restricts its DLL search to System32; viola never holds, queues or re-orders a human key behind a resize and never answers DA1 itself.
Windows is the first target. The Windows, macOS and Linux paths build and pass CI on every commit against the fake agent, so no design choice may depend on tmux, a shell or POSIX-only behaviour.

body_fields.why: the Unix wrapper must put its host terminal into raw mode through termios and restore it on Drop, the Unix leg of the HostTerminal parity the chunk reads.
body_fields.quote: `viola run` puts its own host terminal into raw input + VT output for the run through `HostTerminal` (Windows console modes; Unix termios) and restores the saved modes on Drop — without it ConPTY line-buffers keys until Enter and swallows Ctrl-C; off a terminal it is a no-op.

body_fields.why: the Unix spawn must set the child's cwd explicitly as the Windows spawn does, part of spawn behaving alike on every OS.
body_fields.quote: The child's cwd is set explicitly to viola's current directory (portable-pty 0.8.1 defaults to `%USERPROFILE%`).

body_fields.why: the Unix wrapper's exit must be recorded in the same closed `exit_source` words, so the one diagnostics schema holds on every OS.
body_fields.quote: The exit is recorded as `exit_source` `handle-wait` or `kill-fallback`.

body_fields.why: a Unix parity test of resize then key must wait for the child to see the new size, and the openpty wrapper must never hold a key behind a resize.
body_fields.quote: viola never holds, queues or re-orders a human key behind a resize ([Human Takeover / Wheel]). A test that writes a key after a resize waits for the child to observe the new size first (0 of 200 lost, ci#36529038462).

body_fields.why: on Linux and macOS the backend must report `openpty`, the closed word the one schema carries where Windows reports a ConPTY word.
body_fields.quote: `viola_pty::pty_backend()` reports `conpty-sideload` after a successful pre-load, else `conpty` (Windows) or `openpty`.

body_fields.why: the openpty wrapper must stay silent to DA1 like the Windows one, and the DA1 start stall stays owned by "Windows-only live measurements", outside this chunk.
body_fields.quote: viola stays silent (it never answers DA1 itself); the stall of a `viola run` with no terminal on its stdio is an open product finding, owned by the working-route entry "Windows-only live measurements", blocked on an interactive Windows host.
OPEN — whether the real `claude` loses a key typed right after a resize, and the sideloaded ConPTY's DA1 start stall with no terminal on viola's stdio · owner: "Windows-only live measurements"

body_fields.why: on Linux and macOS the pump and the fake agent must read host stdin through `std::io::stdin()`, the non-Windows leg of the seam.
body_fields.quote: elsewhere, and for a redirected Windows stdin, it is `std::io::stdin()`. Its callers are `run`'s pump and the fake agent.

body_fields.why: any code the openpty path adds must run on std threads with blocking I/O, viola-pty staying a sync crate under the tokio ban and the three-OS cargo check.
body_fields.quote: **[Concurrency / Backend Framework] Hybrid sync core + Tokio only in `mcp` (KEYSTONE).** Rationale: portable-pty's handles are blocking, so the pump needs threads either way. `hook` spawns once per hook event and must not pay for runtime startup. rmcp and interprocess-async require Tokio, so it is confined to the subcommand that uses them. CI enforces this with a sole-root `cargo deny` `tokio` ban (`deny-sync.toml`, run once per crate listed in `scripts/sync-crates.txt`), evaluated for the Windows, macOS and Linux target triples, plus a `cargo check` of the listed sync crates on all three OSes (CI job 3).
CI enforces it with a sole-root `cargo deny` `tokio` ban and a `cargo check` of the sync crates on all three OSes.

body_fields.why: chaos_feed_panic's Unix byte oracle and Windows no-literal oracle must stay split with their reason, the Windows reading left to its owner, not moved to make a Unix case pass.
body_fields.quote: OPEN — on a Windows host, how the child's panicking wide character (`e4 b8 ad`) reaches the outer terminal after a contained vt100 feed panic under a 1-column ConPTY is not read: ConPTY re-renders the child's output, and a wide character on a 1-column screen has no guaranteed rendering, so `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs` asserts those bytes on Unix and, on Windows, only that no viola literal appears on the outer terminal; the reading and a Windows byte oracle from it · owner: "Windows-only live measurements".

body_fields.why: `list --json`'s `skipped` object and its counts must carry the same three fields on every OS, part of the one-schema rule over every `--json` document and `events.ndjson`.
body_fields.quote: The counts are not logged. `viola list` is the first surface that shows them (chunk 2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list): `list --json`'s `skipped` `{unknown_kinds, unknown_fields, torn_lines}` and the BAY line's `skipped a - b - c`, each summed over every scanned instance, gone ones included.
Each event line is one `write`; the next append heals a torn last line, and readers count it and never rewrite the log.

body_fields.why: the Unix suite's socket endpoints on macos-latest must stay inside the macOS socket-path cap, endpoint names hashed and short.
body_fields.quote: Rationale: one API over named pipes and Unix sockets, sync and Tokio flavours, and no daemon. macOS caps socket paths at about 104 bytes.
endpoint names are a short hash of the instance; on Windows the client connects only through the SQOS Identification open, never interprocess's default connect.

body_fields.why: the server pid check must be read on Linux as on Windows, and never on macOS, where no peer pid is reported.
body_fields.quote: `viola_channel::Client::server_pid` and `tokio_client::TokioClient::server_pid` return the connected stream's peer pid through interprocess's `peer_creds().pid()`: Linux `SO_PEERCRED`, Windows `GetNamedPipeServerProcessId` on the client end the SQOS Identification open adopts, none on macOS, where `SERVER_PID_REPORTED` is false; they write and log nothing. Every frame-writing client compares that pid and the process's OS start time with the snapshot's before its first frame (§Standard Contracts, Channel methods), so on Linux and Windows a squatted or rogue server is never sent a frame either.

body_fields.why: macOS must keep its recorded gap, no test reading it as a comparison, and a macOS `server-verify-failed` must mean an euid mismatch alone.
body_fields.quote: On macOS no peer pid is reported, so `viola_state::liveness::server_verdict` returns `Matches` with no comparison: the recorded gap, named and owned by no route entry. The macOS client euid and socket-directory checks, and the 0755-directory exit-cause case, stand built, so on macOS `server-verify-failed` means an euid mismatch alone.

body_fields.why: on Linux and macOS a peer whose euid cannot be read must be refused, and no test seam the Unix suite needs may force that decision.
body_fields.quote: `viola_channel` exports `peer_euid_admitted`, `peer_admitted` and `PEER_EUID_REPORTED`, the last `cfg!(unix)`: `peer_euid_admitted(observed, own, reported)` is `!reported || observed == Some(own)`, so a peer whose euid cannot be read is refused where it is reported, and on Windows the DACL and the pid comparison stay the controls.

body_fields.why: the wrapper's admission must stay injected only through the private `serve_admitting`, so a Unix-only test seam never forces a refusing peer-euid decision.
body_fields.quote: The wrapper's `accept_loop` filters `incoming()` by `admitted(peer_euid_of(stream))`, so a refused stream is dropped on the accept thread, before its worker thread and any frame, reading end-of-file, writing no line, nothing on the terminal and moving no wheel; `Server::serve` injects the decision, `peer_admitted`, as a `type Admission` through the private `serve_admitting`, with no env, flag or feature seam.

body: **[PTY] ↔ [Concurrency / Backend Framework]**: the openpty wrapper on Linux and macOS goes through the same pinned seam, exit read on the process handle, and any code it adds on the `run` or pty path stays on std threads and blocking I/O, viola-pty a sync crate under the sole-root tokio ban checked on all three OSes (architecture/established-decisions fct-ad44nn2e) (architecture/established-decisions fct-gmzv3mtg).

**[PTY] ↔ the diagnostics line schema (the task's `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`)**: the Unix wrapper records its exit as `handle-wait` or `kill-fallback` and its backend as `openpty`, words of the same closed sets the Windows wrapper fills, so no OS-only word or missing key reaches a process-log line (architecture/established-decisions fct-ad44nn2e).

**[Message Broker / IPC] server pid ↔ the macOS carve-out**: Linux parity tests read the pid and start-time server check as Windows ones do, while macOS keeps `Matches` with no comparison and no test reads it as one (architecture/established-decisions fct-rrvv5rrr) (architecture/established-decisions fct-y7p4rnnj).

**[Message Broker / IPC] peer euid ↔ the Decisions Log**: the euid admission stays injected only through the private `serve_admitting`; any Unix-only seam the parity suite needs forces no refusing decision and takes a Decisions Log entry (architecture/established-decisions fct-wqjpkbtb) (architecture/established-decisions fct-ddp4mvl7).

**[PTY] OPEN items ↔ the cfg-reason rule and "Windows-only live measurements"**: a test whose oracle differs per OS, `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs` among them, keeps its split and names its reason where it stands, and its Windows reading, like the DA1 stall and the key-after-resize question, stays with its owner, no Windows pin moved (architecture/established-decisions fct-7xqqphkl) (architecture fct-bq65okf4).

**[Message Broker / IPC] macOS path cap ↔ the test homes (occupied-resources)**: the socket path a macos-latest test home yields stays within about 104 bytes, endpoint names hashed and short (architecture/established-decisions fct-wfmyj5kz) (architecture fct-w2igrcse).

body_fields.why: the CI perf job the chunk re-reads green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest must hold every spine hook within SPINE_DEADLINE, with the hook still exiting 0 on an unreachable endpoint.
body_fields.quote: Each writes its `hook.event` and exits 0 within viola's spine deadline: one built-in value for every event, below the `timeout` (5 s) those hooks get in `hooks.json`. That value is the product constant `viola_core::SPINE_DEADLINE` = 1 s, the bound the perf gate reads (test-plan §10). The connect deadline `viola hook` passes to `Client::connect_by` is the hook-local, crate-private `CONNECT_DEADLINE` = 750 ms (provisional), asserted below `SPINE_DEADLINE` by a unit test. If the endpoint cannot be reached or written within the deadline, the hook records the failure in `diagnostics/` and exits 0.

the sync spine, no reply body, within viola's spine deadline (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop; SessionEnd inside its 1.5 s budget, never raised); async, printing nothing. A lost endpoint loses the event, not the turn.

body_fields.why: the Unix suite's hook paths must run the socket-directory, peer-euid and server checks in this order, each refusal failing open with its closed word, the server check comparing pid and start time on Linux and nothing on macOS.
body_fields.quote: `check_endpoint_dir` on the recorded endpoint, then `Client::connect_by`, then `peer_admitted(client.server_euid())`, then `verify_server` (§Standard Contracts, Session liveness). A refused directory gets no frame: the hook records `socket-dir-refused` and exits 0 with no body. A serving process of another euid, or whose pid or OS start time is not the snapshot's, or a check that cannot be made, gets no frame: the hook records `server-verify-failed` and exits 0 with no body, the event lost as for an unreachable endpoint.

A dialog hook whose server check fails (the serving process is not the recorded wrapper, or the check cannot be made) sends no `hook.dialog` and exits 0 at once with no body, so the dialog renders for the human
**[Message Broker / IPC] interprocess 2.4.4 `local_socket`, one endpoint per `viola run`, behind viola's own `channel` seam.**

body_fields.why: the hook-decision line a refused socket directory or euid writes must carry the same level, fields and closed detail words on Linux and macOS as the diagnostics schema fixes them.
body_fields.quote: `viola hook` meeting a refused socket directory (`NotSent::SocketDir`, `Asked::SocketDir`) exits 0 with empty streams and no frame and writes one `hook-decision` at WARN with `detail` `socket-dir-refused`, on the dialog path after `hook-invoked{corr:null}` with `decision_emitted:false`; a refused euid is `NotSent::ServerUnverified` in the same fail-open form, reading `server-verify-failed`.

body_fields.why: the scope keeps hook's contract on every OS, so no Unix parity change may give hook a stderr byte or a non-zero exit, and its log stays codes-only in its role file.
body_fields.quote: `hook` never writes to stderr. Its codes-only process log goes to the home-level `diagnostics/hook-<name>.ndjson`, and content-bearing detail goes only to the instance's `diagnostics/detail-hook.ndjson` (format owned by obs). A failure to write either is ignored. Rationale: exit 2 is a blocking error in Claude Code's contract, and a viola bug must never block the user's session.
Exit 0 with a JSON body is a decision, with no body no decision; exit 2 is never produced, and `hook` never writes to stderr.

body_fields.why: The v1-40 stale-row witness and the Unix kill-and-revive read must judge liveness exactly as this rule states, heartbeat primary and pid plus start time deciding gone, on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest as on Windows.
body_fields.quote: **[Session Liveness] Heartbeat file primary; pid + process start time decide `gone`, and `claude agents --json` only enriches it.** Rationale: the prototype's heartbeat proved reliable. A bare pid is unsafe because pids get reused, which is why start time is matched too: a snapshot whose pid is dead, or alive with another start time, is `gone` whatever the heartbeat says (Session liveness).
Between the first snapshot and the spawn `run` also rewrites the per-session settings override (Unix only; §Occupied Resources, Claude Code integration names).

**[Session Liveness] Heartbeat file primary; pid + process start time decide `gone`, and `claude agents --json` only enriches it.** A `viola run` or `viola revive` whose `ViolaName` is `live` or `stale` refuses to start; a revive resumes the `gone` instance in place through the same start as `run`, its `events.ndjson` appended to, never truncated.

body_fields.why: The collision check's printed, logged and span words are closed words of tests/run_cli.rs behaviours the Unix suite must read identically on every OS.
body_fields.quote: `collision_check` prints and logs `stale-heartbeat` for a `stale` holder and `already-live` for a live holder or a fresh replayed beat. The `run.collision_check` span's `outcome` reads `already-live` for a live or a stale holder, its closed set saying a holder stands. Stale heartbeat is exit 1's cause alone: a frame verb against a stale instance reads `instance-dead`, `live_endpoint` giving none for a stale wrapper.

`run`'s collision check takes its caller's one snapshot read (`replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`): over a replayed snapshot, which holds no `pid` or `started_at`, it decides from the heartbeat alone, a beat at most `STALE_AFTER` old refusing `already-live` and an older one free; a failed read or no snapshot is free.

body_fields.why: The scope keeps macOS's recorded no-peer-pid gap, so the server check must compare pid and start time on Linux and Windows only and no Unix test may read macOS as a comparison.

body_fields.why: The start's home-tree strict-modes check is an OS-differing rule a parity test must read per OS, with the same refusal pair and the same strict-modes-failed document on Unix as on Windows.

The pure `server_verdict(recorded_pid, started_at, observed_pid, observed_start, peer_pid_reported)` compares the snapshot's `pid` and `started_at` (whole seconds, read through its RFC 3339 form) with the observed peer pid and that process's OS start time; with `peer_pid_reported` false, as on macOS, which reports no peer pid, it returns `Matches` with no comparison: the recorded gap.

body_fields.why: the peer-euid decision is fixed by `cfg!(unix)`, and no Unix test seam the suite adds may force it to refuse.
body_fields.quote: `peer_euid_admitted(observed, own, reported)` is `!reported || observed == Some(own)`, so a peer it cannot read is refused where reported; `peer_admitted(observed)` is that decision over this process's `own_euid()` and `PEER_EUID_REPORTED` (`cfg!(unix)`).

The wrapper touches `<instance dir>/heartbeat` every 1 s. When the snapshot's pid + start time no longer name a running process (the pid is dead, or alive with another start time) the session is `gone`, whatever the beat's age. Otherwise a beat at most 5 s old is `live`, and an older or absent beat is `stale`.

body_fields.why: the snapshots must carry one envelope on every OS, and since a replayed snapshot is never `stale`, the v1-40 witness must stand on a real snapshot with an old beat.
body_fields.quote: A snapshot whose `v` is higher than the reader supports, or that fails to parse, is ignored, and the state is rebuilt by replaying `events.ndjson`. Unix domain socket file `<socket dir>/viola-<h12>.sock` in a per-user 0700 directory, never the `/tmp` or `$TMPDIR` root, checked before the bind and before every client's connect and, when refused (`socket-dir-refused`), left as found, never narrowed;

body_fields.why: The perf job re-read green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest must produce all five perf exports that `gate --require perf` requires.
body_fields.quote: `artifacts/` holds the per-suite JUnit, `run-summary.json`, `llvm-cov-summary.json` (from `run --coverage`) and the five `perf-<hook>.json` hyperfine exports (from `run --perf`, one per timed row, each required by `gate --require perf`); the perf session's `<session>/` also holds its synthetic `payload-<hook>.json` inputs.

Its hyperfine exports are `target/agent-run/artifacts/perf-<hook>.json`, one per row (`session-start`, `user-prompt-submit`, `stop`, `session-end`, `pre-tool-use`), all five required by `gate --require perf` (obs-plan §9); the perf session boots unstamped.

body_fields.why: The obs gates G1 to G4 the chunk re-reads green on Unix read exactly these kept homes, the one chaos home outside them.
body_fields.quote: every harness and test home but the one `viola-chaos-*` home of `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs` (Filesystem, above), gitignored and kept in CI for the obs gates (never under `run --mutants`, which keeps no home).
`v1-47`'s after every end-to-end test is after each job's end-to-end run: `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` `"1"` on the job and `if: always()` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, the `viola-chaos-*` home out.
Its forced vt100 feed panic writes a G2-counted `event:"panic"` line, so the home sits outside `target/e2e-home` and therefore outside G2 (zero panics), G4 (schema conformance) and the secret scan;

body_fields.why: The Linux suite runs on the dev host go through the linked base, so a stamped-home gate there must first meet the headroom floor (the directive's `df -h /tmp` read), while CI runners have no link.
body_fields.quote: A linked base whose filesystem reads less than `HEADROOM_FLOOR_MIB` (9 GiB) free by `statvfs` (`f_bavail × f_frsize`) is refused too, with the fixed message `e2e-home backing: {free} MiB free, below the {floor} MiB floor` (the two counts, no path);

Test-only, outside the repository, on the Linux dev host only: `/tmp/viola-e2e-home-<uid>/` (mode 0700, owned by the user), the tmpfs directory the dev host's `target/e2e-home` link points at, holding every test and session home of that host. `viola` never reads or writes it by that name. No CI runner has it.

body: **res-filesystem strict-modes rules ↔ Cross-cutting Patterns (cross-platform discipline)**: each per-OS leg of the strict-modes check (the role file's read rule on Unix, write rule on Windows; mode bits against ACEs; a regular file above a checked path) must be tested on its own CI runner, a Unix case on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest and a Windows case staying cfg(windows) with its reason named where it stands (architecture/occupied-resources fct-wdtionxy) (architecture/occupied-resources fct-kekl3p46) (architecture/occupied-resources fct-sbmskf35) (architecture/occupied-resources fct-hn66ngvt) (architecture fct-fa2klbw5)

**res-filesystem diag-line closed words ↔ Conventions (data model)**: the one-schema rule holds diag-line.v1.json's closed enums and the process-exit refusal codes to one closed set on every OS, and a field one OS cannot fill is omitted or null, never an OS-only word (architecture/occupied-resources fct-gftfjtay) (architecture/occupied-resources fct-if66544y) (architecture fct-u5xw5irn)

**res-filesystem test homes ↔ obs gates G1 to G4 and the ci.yml re-read**: the Unix test and perf jobs keep every test home under `target/e2e-home` (`AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES`, `if: always()`) so G1 to G4 read them green beside windows-2025, the chaos home outside G2 and G4, and the perf job yields all five exports `gate --require perf` requires (architecture/occupied-resources fct-xib5fpty) (architecture/occupied-resources fct-x2qzlbqt) (architecture/occupied-resources fct-fs7kfa27) (architecture fct-swegdoif)

**res-filesystem kill support ↔ Standard Contracts (session liveness)**: the Unix kill-and-revive reading waits on `holder_gone` within `WITHIN` = 7 s and reads the child gone by pid and start time, while `run_child_ends_when_its_wrapper_is_terminated` stays cfg(windows) (architecture/occupied-resources fct-jv5gqhbl) (architecture/occupied-resources fct-flit34us) (architecture fct-arftgre4)

**res-filesystem `viola list` read rule and res-env-vars colour names ↔ Standard Contracts (session liveness)**: the v1-40 witness must run `viola list` on a home at the read rule, with `NO_COLOR` absent and `TERM` not `dumb` so SGR bytes are written, beside a wrapper whose heartbeat is older than 5 s (architecture/occupied-resources fct-isxdwj6d) (architecture fct-lak6evbp) (architecture fct-arftgre4)

**res-filesystem socket roots ↔ res-ipc-endpoints (Unix socket)**: the per-OS socket root (`TMPDIR` on macOS, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` on Linux) gives each Unix test its own per-user socket directory, never the `/tmp` or `$TMPDIR` root (architecture/occupied-resources fct-5v4ir6ih) (architecture fct-wular7qm)

body_fields.why: any Unix-only test seam the parity suite needs must join this closed list, compiled only under the fake-agent feature, and the v1-40 witness's SGR bytes are decided only by the three colour variables it names.
body_fields.quote: The only other variables any `viola` build reads are the two test seams `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` (capped at 5 s) and `FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC` (exact value `1`, a forced fail-open `hook` panic), both compiled only under `cfg(feature = "fake-agent")` and absent from release builds, and, in every build, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM`, read by viola's own colour layer (`src/human/style.rs`, `viola list`'s human mode only) to decide whether and how deep its SGR bytes are written (the founder's own word, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline): they configure nothing, disable no control and widen no redaction.
There are no secrets in v1, and environment variables are not a configuration channel: a dependency or feature that reads one breaks this rule like a direct read does.

body_fields.why: the Unix R8 pass-list is a per-OS behaviour that a parity test must read on the Unix runners as Unix-only, without making it a Windows behaviour or an OS-only schema word.
body_fields.quote: and `claude_env_keep` (the Unix R8 pass-list of `CLAUDE*` names, default empty)

body_fields.why: the chunk reads v1-53's live Linux leg against what earlier chunks measured live on the Linux dev host, and this row records that measurement while the CI runners read the behaviour under the fake agent only.
body_fields.quote: `viola revive`'s: `claude --resume <id>` reopens the same session and fires a SessionStart of source `resume` with that id (as measured on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host at chunk 2026-10-10-viola-revive, `evidence/live-revive.md`, three live starts; the CI runners read it under the fake agent only).

The first live run was on the Linux dev host, by the founder's ruling R-L1 (2026-10-07, relayed by the overseer), at chunk 2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive (`claude` 2.1.287 in foot 1.28.0 under Hyprland 0.56.2); Windows live behaviour stays proven on the CI runner under the fake agent until an interactive Windows host exists.

body_fields.why: the statusline rows are relied on Unix only, so the relied set differs per OS, and a parity test stamping a test home for the fake agent must read its own OS's relied set and leave the Windows legs owed where they stand.
body_fields.quote: Their rows landed at chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows: `statusline-override`, `statusline-shell` and `statusline-rate-limits`, probed by Run B's probe `--settings` ([CLI Version Compatibility]), relied on Unix only and stamped live on 2.1.287 on the Linux dev host (`stamped 2.1.287  21 pass  0 fail`, `evidence/live-round.md`), with the two `StatusLine` fixtures, so `budget-paused` now rests on a stamped row; the Windows legs stay owed to "Windows-only live measurements" (the operator's direction at the 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through wrap). The dialog answer mapping (the S3/S7/S8 decision bodies) is gated by its own rows (`question-answer` · `plan-approve-revise` · `question-notes` · `dialog-concurrency`) inside the relied-set `cli_verified` (`LedgerRow::relied()`: 24 rows on Unix, 21 on Windows; [CLI Version Compatibility]).
Nothing shells out through `sh`, `bash` or `cmd`, except `hook statusline` running the user's own statusline command (see Hook contract).

body_fields.why: every product reader of external bytes that the openpty wrapper path adds must be bounded in its own statement or named in an EXCEPTIONS row of tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs.
body_fields.quote: Every product reader of external bytes is bounded in the same statement (`take`) or named in an `EXCEPTIONS` row; none reads an external byte source to its end unbounded.

Every product reader of external bytes is bounded in its own statement (`take`) or named as an exception (the own-executable reads); the contract binary `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs` enumerates the boundaries and censuses the product sources.
New code on the `run`, `hook`, `send` or channel-server paths uses std threads and blocking I/O.

body_fields.why: the chunk re-asserts that every --json document carries the same closed words on every OS, and this rule keeps those words closed, with no path or upstream text on any OS.
body_fields.quote: CLI `--json` documents, MCP error results and channel error data carry codes and fixed messages only, no path and no upstream text; a peer's `message`, `data`, `refusal` or `detail` reaches no document or text but as a closed value, and a code word outside the closed list stays visible by design.

body_fields.why: every exit-21 cause and exit-1 code the Unix suite reaches, socket-dir-refused included, must be the same row of tests/contract_error_bodies.rs on every OS, with no OS-only code word.
body_fields.quote: Every exit-21 cause and exit-1 code passes `is_code_word` and is a row of `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs`, carrying no path, pid or upstream text.

body_fields.why: the socket-directory refusal belongs to the Unix endpoint, so its human pair is a Unix surface that the parity suite must read as written.
body_fields.quote: The `unable:` / `hint:` pair for a socket directory names only the parsed `ViolaName`, no path, pid or uid, is plain ASCII with `hint:` last and no SGR, its hint `send_hint`'s cause `socket-dir` in `src/human/hints.rs`.

body: **Config management (closed variable list) ↔ Conventions (environment-variable naming) and the scope's test-seam boundary**: a Unix-only test seam the parity suite needs joins the closed list of variables a viola build reads, compiled only under `cfg(feature = "fake-agent")` and absent from release builds (architecture/crosscut-config fct-k6htnrfj). It must fit the naming rule's ratified test-seam exceptions (architecture fct-qqxg3ika), take a Decisions Log entry, and never force a refusing peer-euid decision.

**Config management (colour variables) ↔ Standard Contracts (Session liveness) and Occupied Resources (environment variables)**: the v1-40 integration-tier witness reads SGR dim under the outer PTY. Its bytes are decided only by `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and `COLORTERM`, which the test sets in the environment it starts `viola list` with, never viola (architecture/crosscut-config fct-k6htnrfj). The board width comes from `viola_pty::host_size()` (architecture fct-lak6evbp), and the row is stale only past a 5 s beat (architecture fct-arftgre4).

**Capability ledger (live Linux records) ↔ Design Philosophy (first live run on Linux)**: v1-53's live Linux leg is read only against the live measurements on the Linux dev host recorded in the ledger rows (architecture/crosscut-capability-ledger fct-wfge3rsz) and the first live run (architecture fct-igbvtfv6). The Unix CI runners read the same behaviours under the fake agent only, and the chunk starts no live `claude`.

**Capability ledger (Unix-only relied rows) ↔ Occupied Resources (per-session settings override) and Standard Contracts (hook statusline)**: the relied set is 24 rows on Unix and 21 on Windows (architecture/crosscut-capability-ledger fct-wfge3rsz), because the settings override is written only on Unix (architecture fct-klpb7auf) and the `/bin/sh -c` shell-out happens only on Unix (architecture fct-horlp4ay). A parity test reading them is a per-OS test that carries its one-OS reason where it stands, and no Windows pin moves.

**Bounded readers ↔ Established Decisions ([PTY] seam, Tokio containment)**: the openpty backend's read path behind the `pty` seam (architecture fct-omwrdnlc) adds no product reader of external bytes unless it is bounded in its own statement or named in `EXCEPTIONS` (architecture/crosscut-bounded-readers fct-qip7sr3o). It uses std threads and blocking I/O in the sync `viola-pty` crate (architecture fct-me2myqzf).

**Sanitised error surfaces ↔ Standard Contracts (CLI `--json` output) and the scope's one-schema rule**: the closed `UnreachableCause` words, `socket-dir-refused` among them (architecture fct-ksmkl4jd), and `viola revive`'s refusal codes (architecture fct-54jxzo44) read the same on every OS as rows of `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` (architecture/crosscut-sanitised-error-surfaces fct-7ok4646z). A cause that one OS cannot reach still adds no OS-only word.

body:
Brings Linux and macOS to parity with Windows: the `viola run` wrapper there runs its child under portable-pty's openpty backend through the same `pty` seam as ConPTY (spawn, read, write, resize, wait, kill behaving as the Windows wrapper's do under the fake agent).
Makes the full fake-agent suite one suite on all three OSes: every end-to-end and integration test reading a behaviour both Unix OSes share runs on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest, and any test left cfg(windows), cfg(unix) or cfg(target_os) carries its one-OS reason where it stands.
Keeps one diagnostics schema across OSes: process-log lines, events.ndjson, the snapshots and every --json document carry the same fields and closed words, a field one OS cannot fill reading its documented null or closed word.
Adds the integration-tier witness of v1-40 (dim only on stale rows) under the outer PTY on the Unix suite, and re-reads the obs gates G1 to G4 and the CI test, perf and lint jobs green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest beside windows-2025.
Windows stays the live-supported target: no Windows behaviour, pin or test moves; no live claude session runs; macOS keeps its recorded no-peer-pid gap.

body_fields.what: the test, perf and lint jobs over the three OSes (their matrix.os), read green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest beside windows-2025

body: The PTY decision and its pty seam (spawn, read, write, resize, wait, kill) over portable-pty pinned =0.8.1, here its openpty backend on Linux and macOS: child exit is detected on the process handle, never on EOF; viola never holds, queues or re-orders a human key behind a resize and never answers DA1 itself.

The fake agent as the CI stand-in: the test-only viola-fake-agent bin behind feature fake-agent, its control and receipt files under a test home's fake/ dir, the committed fake-script scenarios, and the test seams FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS and FAKE_AGENT_HOOK_PANIC read only under that feature.

The CI/CD decision the Unix suite runs under: the GitHub Actions three-OS matrix against the fake agent, the fake agent named after `--`, the child resolved to an absolute path and spawned directly, each test in its own viola home through --home so parallel tests share no endpoint, log or budget.json.

The obs gates G1 bare instrument, G2 zero panics, G3 no abort panic strategy and G4 schema conformance, read over the test homes under target/e2e-home kept in CI, with the viola-chaos home the named carve-out outside G2, G4 and the secret scan.

The diagnostics line schemas diag-line.v1.json and diag-detail.v1.json (obs-owned, default-deny, pinned by tests/contract_diag_schema.rs) and the role files under diagnostics/: codes only, one line per write, the same on every OS.

The own-format contracts the one-schema rule covers: the ndjson event line and its per-kind data, the snapshot envelope and the instance snapshot fields, and the CLI --json documents with their closed error and detail words (UnreachableCause, revive refusal codes).

Indirect, through the data model conventions: optional fields are omitted on write and readers treat missing and null the same, so a field one OS cannot fill must still read its documented null or closed word under that convention, never an OS-only word.

The Linux and macOS IPC endpoint: the Unix socket viola-<h12>.sock in a per-user 0700 socket dir (never the /tmp or $TMPDIR root, checked before bind and every connect, socket-dir-refused left as found), chmod 0600 after bind, both sides admitting only the owning user's euid.

The macOS carve-out: macOS reports no peer pid, so the server check a frame-writing client makes against the snapshot's pid and started_at compares nothing there; that check runs on Linux and Windows only, and no test reads macOS as a comparison.

Indirect, through the peer-euid check: no env, flag or feature seam may force a refusing peer-euid decision, and any Unix-only test seam the suite needs takes a Decisions Log entry and must fit the naming rule's ratified test-seam exceptions.

Session liveness as the v1-40 witness reads it: the heartbeat touched every 1 s, a beat older than 5 s stale, pid plus process start time deciding gone; a viola list beside a stale wrapper reads SGR dim across the whole row, NAME dim and bold.
The human output colour decision viola list makes under the outer PTY: NO_COLOR, TERM and COLORTERM read never set, deciding only the SGR bytes, and the board width taken from viola_pty::host_size().

The kill-and-revive test support: Wrapper::kill in tests/support/home.rs and the root Watch bound WITHIN of 7 s with its viola-root-watch evidence report, by which a killed wrapper's child is read gone by pid and start time on Unix; the standalone pin run_child_ends_when_its_wrapper_is_terminated stays cfg(windows).

OS-differing behaviours a parity test must read per OS: the strict-modes rules (Unix no group or other bit, Windows the DACL; events.ndjson the write rule on Unix, the read rule on Windows), the per-session settings.json override written only on Unix, hook statusline's /bin/sh -c shell-out (none on Windows) and the claude_env_keep Unix R8 pass-list.

The cross-platform discipline: every OS-specific branch compiles and is tested on its CI runner, nothing shells out but hook statusline, child processes are spawned directly, endpoint names hashed and short.
Indirect, through Tokio containment and the sync crates: any new code on the run or pty path uses std threads and blocking I/O, viola-pty staying a sync crate under the sole-root tokio ban.

Indirect, through the bounded readers rule: any product reader of external bytes the openpty path adds is bounded in its own statement or named as an exception, censused by tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs.
The typed exit-code set stays 0, 1, 2, 10 to 14, 20, 21, and viola hook keeps its contract: always exit 0, no body when no decision, nothing on stderr.

The wheel's closed non-editing list as the CARRY names it: measured only on foot 1.28.0; a terminal answering CSI ? 6 n or the kitty graphics APC query writes a reply that still counts as typing, and a shape joins the list only when measured by its exact grammar on the founder's word.

The test-only channel endpoints viola-test-chan-<pid>-<label> (a socket of that base name off Windows) and the viola-pty-watch report files of the real-PTY tests, whose dsr-cpr count reads the CSI 6 n queries the rig saw.

The capabilities this entry answers to: v1-53 (Linux and macOS reach parity with Windows: the parity suite, the macOS gap record, the live Linux leg read against earlier live runs) and v1-40's integration-tier witness.

The cross-platform design philosophy: Windows first, all three OS paths built and CI-tested on every commit against the fake agent, no design choice depending on tmux, a shell or POSIX-only behaviour; the first live run was on the Linux dev host.

body_fields.convention: every new test runs in its own viola home through --home, under target/e2e-home (viola-test-*), kept in CI for the obs gates, a new home removing only dirs whose recorded owner process is gone
every new end-to-end or integration test drives the fake agent named after `--`, never the real claude in CI
every OS-specific branch or cfg-gated test compiles and is tested on its own CI runner
test-harness-only variables carry the AGENT_RUN_ prefix and are never read by viola; a test seam is read only under cfg(feature = "fake-agent") and absent from release builds
every new log line is codes only, one complete JSON object per write, in its role file under diagnostics/ and conforming to diag-line.v1.json; content-bearing detail only in the instance detail files
every new test-only endpoint or evidence file sits outside the viola-<h12> namespace, unique per test (pid and label), its report kept when the test panics or is killed and removed when it passes
every new path a test or job writes under target/ is gitignored and recorded in Occupied Resources' Repository list
every new fake-agent scenario is a committed synthetic-only script validated against schemas/fake-script.v1.json

The frontend and the GUI control scope, deferred to 0.2.0.
The dialog answer mapping and the answer, hook.dialog and permission continuation contracts; the chunk changes no dialog behaviour.
The separate fuzz workspace, its nightly toolchain, targets and corpus, and the nightly fuzz job.

Hosting, mobile, AI/ML and public distribution (dist releases, signing, winget, Homebrew, Scoop, self_update): none apply to v1 parity.

body: **2026-09-24-three-os-ci-headless-harness-skeleton** (CI setup and wired jobs; test-only crate, bins, env vars, paths) — CI installs the toolchain by `rustup toolchain install` with SHA-pinned actions and `permissions: {}`; the `test` job was born as the 3-OS harness leg. Registered `viola-fake-agent` (feature `fake-agent`), `viola-harness`, the `AGENT_RUN_` prefix and `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES`, home-level `diagnostics/` and `target/e2e-home/`. Why it matters: the three-OS matrix and its native runners are the base this chunk reads green on both Unix legs; any harness-only variable the parity suite needs falls under the `AGENT_RUN_` rule, not a new `VIOLA_*`.

**2026-09-24-fake-agent-and-test-data-fixtures** — Named the root rstest homes `viola-test-*/home` beside the harness `viola-session-*/home`, and made `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES` read by the root test chain too. Why it matters: the test-home layout under `target/e2e-home/` that G1 to G4 read on the Unix runners rests on this split.

**2026-09-24-supply-chain-and-workflow-gates** — The tokio ban became `deny-sync.toml` run once per crate in `scripts/sync-crates.txt` as the sole root (an excluded-graph check false-failed under feature unification); `ci.yml` is the push/PR workflow, `nightly.yml` the weekly one. Why it matters: any code the openpty path adds stays inside a sync crate under this ban, checked for all three target triples; the chunk adds no workflow beside `ci.yml`.

**2026-09-24-diagnostics-plane** — Process-log lines carry no `v` (their version lives in the schema filename); every role's codes-only log goes to its home-level role file; `schemas/diag-line.v1.json` and `schemas/diag-detail.v1.json` registered. Why it matters: the chunk's one-schema rule holds these line schemas identical on every OS, the `v` exception included.

**2026-09-24-observability-gates** — Added the `print_stdout` / `print_stderr` / `dbg_macro` bans, ripgrep 15.2.0 for G1/G3 (via `scripts/install-ripgrep.sh`), runner `jq` for G2 and jsonschema 0.57.0 for `schema-check` (G4); the `test` job follows the obs gate order with scan-gated uploads and the `lint` job wires G1/G3. Why it matters: these tools must be present and green on `ubuntu-latest` and `macos-latest` for the gates the chunk re-reads.

**2026-09-24-quality-gates** — Wired coverage (cargo-llvm-cov) into the `test` job and recorded the declined `concurrency:` block with its reason. Why it matters: the per-OS coverage floors read under `gate --require coverage` and the standing no-`concurrency:` rule both bind the chunk's CI acceptance.

**2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows** — The wrapper as built: R8 became a `CLAUDE*` prefix rule (case-insensitive on Windows, `config.json` `claude_env_keep` on Unix), [PTY] recorded `HostTerminal` raw mode, explicit child cwd and viola-side program resolution, `viola-pty` deps portable-pty, windows-sys (Windows) and libc (Unix), and `PtyError` became the one ratified thiserror exception. Why it matters: the openpty leg runs behind this same seam and error type; the R8 strip and `HostTerminal` are per-OS behaviours a parity test must read per OS.

**2026-09-26-local-linux-pre-push-gate** — `FAKE_AGENT_PUMP_DELAY_MS` ratified as the one exception to the `VIOLA_` / `AGENT_RUN_` rule: read only under `cfg(feature = "fake-agent")`, capped, absent from release builds, a boundary widening ratified at wrap. Why it matters: the precedent and form for any Unix-only test seam the parity suite needs, which the scope says takes a Decisions Log entry.

**2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order** — [Session Liveness]: pid + start time decide `gone` whatever the beat, the same process `live` (beat at most 5 s) or `stale`; the start order as landed; `target/e2e-home` gained the owner record and the gone-owner sweep. Why it matters: the kill-and-revive CARRY and the `v1-40` stale-row witness both rest on this liveness rule on Unix.

body:
Brings Linux and macOS to parity with Windows: the `viola run` wrapper runs its child under portable-pty's openpty backend behind the same pty seam as ConPTY (spawn, read, write, resize, wait, kill behave as on Windows, as the fake agent reads them).
Makes the full fake-agent suite one suite on all three OSes: every end-to-end and integration test of a behaviour both Unix OSes share runs on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest; a test left cfg(windows), cfg(unix) or cfg(target_os) names the reason its behaviour is one OS's where it stands.
Re-reads the obs gates G1 to G4 and the CI test, perf and lint jobs green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest beside windows-2025, and re-asserts one diagnostics schema: process-log lines, events.ndjson, snapshots and every --json document carry the same fields and closed words on every OS.
Takes up the carried integration-tier witness of v1-40: under the outer PTY a `viola list` beside a stale wrapper reads SGR dim across the whole row, NAME dim and bold.
Windows stays the live-supported target: no Windows behaviour, pin or test moves; no live claude session, everything on the fake agent; no new exit code.

body_fields.what: the test, perf and lint jobs over matrix.os reading green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest beside windows-2025

body: The cli surface's platform list: macOS and Linux terminals are supported beside Windows Terminal and conhost, so every human output pattern of the cli surface must print the same lines on Unix as on Windows.

The cli colour decision order (first match wins: --json, viola run, hook and mcp, NO_COLOR, TERM=dumb, stdout not a terminal, Windows VT enable failed): on Unix the Windows VT step never applies, and the depth choice (COLORTERM truecolor or 24bit, TERM containing 256color, else the 16-colour fallback) is what a Unix test under openpty reads.

The cli tokens for a stale row: SGR dim on the whole stale row, bold NAME, the DIALOG word amber with its kind word and the cock winning over dim, a reset after every styled span, no background ever set; the v1-40 witness reads these bytes from the row's first byte to its last under the outer PTY.

The viola list component pattern: the BAY line, six fixed columns, rows ordered by name, the UNWRAPPED read-only separator, stale liveness after a heartbeat older than 5 s, control characters escaped as \xHH; the Unix suite's list cases read the same board as Windows'.

viola run and a passed viola revive print nothing once the child starts and emit no colour, glyph or cursor control: the openpty wrapper's passthrough must keep the child's terminal untouched exactly as the ConPTY wrapper does.

The cli width rule: COLUMNS is never read, only stdout's own terminal width counts and a piped stdout has none, so only an unwrapped NAME is cut and only where that width is known; a Unix test under openpty sets the PTY size, never COLUMNS, and lines are never wrapped.

The viola send readback mirror ([RB], [  ], [/ ], unconfirmable) and its stdout and stderr split, plus the wait and last result lines and their message-mode escaper: the shared fake-agent send, wait and last cases read these same lines and the same exit codes on Unix.
Exit-code phraseology: the typed set stays 0, 1, 2, 10 to 14, 20, 21 with each code's human stderr form and --json document; hook still exits 0 with no body and no stderr, mcp writes MCP frames only.

The closed words every --json document carries, the same on every OS: exit 21's six detail causes (strict-modes-failed, instance-dead, unwrapped-name, endpoint-lost, server-verify-failed, socket-dir-refused) and revive's start refusal codes; a case one OS cannot fill reads the documented null or closed word, never a missing key or an OS-only word.

The strict-modes refusals' fixed home-state and instance-state unable: and hint: pairs (list, plugin install, link, unlink, send, wait, last, answer, pause, release) and the run and revive start refusals' fixed-message lines: on Unix they print the same fixed text, with no path and no pid.
Diagnostics home: stack traces never print and full detail goes only to instances/<name>/diagnostics/; the per-OS diagnostics schema the chunk re-asserts is that home's content.
Platform-Specific Notes: the Git Bash rewritten-path warning and conhost-without-VT fallback are Windows-only behaviours, the named reason a test of them may stay cfg(windows).
Human output is ASCII only (->, [RB], [/ ], [  ], two spaces between columns, no link column in viola list) on every OS, in piped, NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb output too.

body_fields.convention: each new error, refusal or hint line a test, seam or wrapper path adds is a fixed message that prints no upstream text, path, pid, anyhow chain or stack trace; full detail goes to diagnostics only

each new test that reads human CLI output keeps results on stdout and waiting, refusal, hint and error lines on stderr, and expects no colour, glyph or cursor control under --json, non-TTY, NO_COLOR, TERM=dumb or viola run

The Self-Validation Protocol's swap, squint, token and sameness tests: checks of a new visual design, and this chunk designs no new interface.
Rejected Defaults and the Universal Bans on decorative colour and convergent choices: the chunk adds no styled element and no new visual state.

body: **2026-09-28-cli-output-tokens** — clap built without `color`, so every styled byte of human output is viola's own SGR module's. `CLICOLOR_FORCE` could otherwise force SGR into a pipe. Witnessed by `cli_output_plain`, green on 3 OSes. This is why a Unix SGR assertion (the v1-40 witness, the pipe/`NO_COLOR`/`TERM=dumb` no-SGR cases) reads that module alone. Re-enabling `color` reopens the ban.

**2026-10-04-wait-and-last** — gave message mode its rule: every control character but `\n`/`\t` prints as `\xHH`, never stripped, and `--json` stays serde-escaped. Unix `wait`/`last`/`link` cases must read the same escaped bytes as Windows (later reused for `link`'s non-RFC-3339 `since`).

**2026-10-06-local-command-send-outcomes** — the readback box also fills on `/clear`'s measured post-condition (a `session-start` of cause `clear`), printing `[RB] read back` with no new word. The shared fake-agent send cases on Unix read the same `[RB]`/`[  ]` mirror outcomes.

**2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive** — reworded the `not-delivered · input-not-ready` hint (founder's wording). This chunk also carries that chunk's reply-probe CARRY. An exit-13 hint the Unix send cases read must print these exact words on every OS.

**2026-10-09-epoch-3-cleanup** — added `empty-text` as an exit-13 detail word, with its hint, after `control-character`. This is part of the closed exit-13 list, which the one-schema re-assertion must find identical on Linux, macOS and Windows.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** — added `revive`'s refusal pairs and its `--list` line form (`<time>  <cause>  <session id>`, plain ASCII). It also put a passed `viola revive` beside `viola run` in the 0.0 expression row and the no-colour ban. So the openpty wrapper must keep revive's passthrough (nothing printed once the child starts) exactly as ConPTY does.

**2026-10-10-budget-governor** — added the `release --budget` lines (`budget gate lifted until <end>` with the `HH:MM:SSZ` / dated forms, `budget gate open`). It also ruled that `revive`'s strict-modes refusal carries no log detail code. The Unix suite re-reads this unstyled line byte for byte.

**2026-10-11-the-board-viola-list** — the board as built: `escape_row` escapes every control character as `\xHH`, WHEEL is padded to 23, there are five board forms, and `list`'s exit-21 whole-board refusal uses the home/instance `unable:`/`hint:` pairs. Unix list cases and the v1-40 witness rest on these fixed columns and pairs.

**2026-10-13-t06-38-35-wrap** — the founder ratified WHEEL 23, the five board forms, `list`'s exit-21 pairs and the two `release --budget` lines. These are founder wording, not planning forms. A Unix case must not alter them to pass.

**2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup** — a `verify` stopped by Ctrl-C/TERM prints no step line and no summary, only the fixed pair `unable: verify was stopped before it finished` / `hint: run viola verify again to stamp this CLI`, and exits 1. On Unix, signal delivery differs from Windows, but this pair must still read identically.

body_fields.why: G1 must read green on both Unix OSes, its SHA-pinned PCRE2 ripgrep install proven by rg --pcre2-version there, so a missing rg fails closed rather than passing.
body_fields.quote:
- **G1, bare `#[instrument]`.**
  - Needs ripgrep built with PCRE2. The runner images do not guarantee `rg`, so a SHA-pinned install step before G1/G3 installs an official ripgrep release binary (release binaries are built with PCRE2) and then runs `rg --pcre2-version` as its own check. Without that step `rg` exits 127, so G1/G3 fail closed on every commit rather than passing.
  - `-U` lets `\s*` span lines, so an `#[instrument(` with `skip_all` on the next line passes. `skip_all` must be the first argument (the §4 form).
  - rg exit 1 (no match) passes. Exit 0 (a violation) and exit 2 (a regex or I/O error) both fail the step. This replaces the earlier `(?!.*skip_all)` form: without `--pcre2` it exits 2 with empty stdout, so a "must be empty" check would pass on every commit.
- **G1, bare `#[instrument]`:** `skip_all` must be the first argument; only rg exit 1 (no match) passes, so a violation, a regex or I/O error and a missing `rg` all fail the step.

Only the output modules that own `--json`, human CLI stderr and the hook decision body may carry a local `#[allow]`, and only where they use a print macro — `run`'s and `revive`'s pre-spawn refusals, `revive --list`'s, `verify`'s, `list`'s and `plugin install`'s refusals, and the instance-check refusal of `link` / `unlink` and of `send` / `wait` / `last` / `answer` / `pause` / `release`, write through `src/human.rs` (`refuse` / `write_refusal`, one `write_all` on the locked stderr; callers `run` 8 · `verify` 6 · `list` 2 · `revive` 1 · `plugin install` 1 · `client` 1, the one `refuse_untrusted` site `link` / `unlink` and the six frame verbs share; the rule: the `human::refuse(` call sites under `src/`), which uses no print macro and carries no `#[allow]` — plus the fake agent's crate-level `#![allow]` in `src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs` (a root-package bin, §3 obs-ci-gate-wire).

A clippy `disallowed-macros` / `print_stdout` / `print_stderr` / `dbg_macro` failure; a `scripts/lint-probes.sh` failure (a ban that did not fire, a control that did not pass, or a raw `event!` outside `crates/viola-core/src/obs.rs`); a G1 bare-`#[instrument]` or G3 `panic = "abort"` hit, or either gate exiting with anything other than rg exit 1 (including exit 2 regex/I-O error and 127 missing `rg`); or a `cargo deny` (Tokio, C-crate, veil `toggle`, banned obs crates) failure.

- NEVER skip the zero-unlogged-panics invariant.

- NEVER log a line per heartbeat tick. Log transitions and lifecycle only, because the files are never rotated.

body_fields.why: On both Unix OSes every role must install the panic hook first and make its home-tree check before any role file opens, so a refusal writes no line, which the Unix suite reads.
body_fields.quote:
Init order per process:
1. As the first statement in `main`, install a replacement panic hook that writes one JSON line and nothing to stderr. The default hook's stderr output breaks the hook contract and the `run` terminal.
2. Parse clap.
3. Resolve the home (`--home`, then the grandparent of `VIOLA_DIR`, then the default) and the instance (`VIOLA_NAME` or an argument). Where the role checks the home before its first open, that strict-modes check runs here — every `viola hook` arm but the two `--capture` arms (`canonical` + `trusted`); `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link` and `unlink` (`refuse_untrusted`); `verify` (`check_home_tree`); `run` and `viola revive`'s start (`checked_exe` + `check_home_tree`) — and a refusal ends the process with nothing under the home opened and no line.
4. Open `diagnostics/<process file>` in append mode with 0600 permissions inside a 0700 directory.
5. Install the subscriber with an explicit writer (never stdout).
6. Emit `process-start`.

body_fields.why: Each line must stay one `write` on an append-mode handle on both Unix OSes, where concurrent hooks share one file under the Unix suite.
body_fields.quote: The writer must emit each formatted line as a single `write` on an append-mode handle (arch Crash-safe disk writes). Concurrent `hook` processes share one file.

body_fields.why: These required fields and the closed `event` enum are the one diagnostics schema the chunk must re-assert on every OS, with no OS-only word.
body_fields.quote:
**Required fields:**
- For process logs: `timestamp` (RFC 3339 UTC with ms and `Z`), `level` (`DEBUG|INFO|WARN|ERROR`), `target`, and `fields.message` (or the flattened `message`).
- `event`, a closed kebab-case enum. A new value needs a Decisions Log entry, like the §3 closed enums. Each value fixes what its `corr` holds:
  - `channel-request`, `channel-response`: `corr` = the JSON-RPC request `id`
  - `dialog-raised`, `dialog-answered`: `corr` = `dialog_id`
  - `hook-invoked`, `hook-decision`: `corr` = `dialog_id` for dialog hooks, otherwise null
