body_fields.why: socket-dir-refused is a Unix-reached logged detail (exit 1 at run and revive's start, exit 21 at the CLI frame verbs) with no path, pid or uid, while a strict-modes refusal before any log opens must write no line.
body_fields.quote: a strict-modes refusal made before any process log opens (the six frame verbs and `link` / `unlink`, exit 21; `run`, `revive`'s start and `verify`, exit 1) writes no line and carries no logged `detail` code: its machine-readable form is the exit code, and under `--json` the closed `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed` (the frame verbs and `link` / `unlink`) or the `strict-modes-failed` document (`revive`); a refused socket directory is outside that exception: it carries the logged `detail` `socket-dir-refused`, no path, pid or uid, exit 21 at the eight CLI frame verbs and exit 1 at `run` and `revive`'s start |

body: **telemetry-strategy multi-platform-exporter-compat ↔ log-coverage required fields and null encoding**: the one sink and line schema on every OS (obs-plan/telemetry-strategy fct-6isebxud) must be met by the same required fields on every line, a field one OS cannot fill encoded by key absence, never an OS-only word (obs-plan fct-qaeihrqm), checked by G4 default-deny against both schemas (obs-plan fct-llmksgvm).

**telemetry-strategy Errors ↔ error-capture-reporting and ci-integration G2**: the Unix run PTY pump and handle-wait threads each inside catch_unwind (obs-plan/telemetry-strategy fct-6c7xwzms) must meet the catch-site rule that no worker panic leaves main running without its process-exit and every profile keeps unwind (obs-plan fct-sue3fxzz), counted by G2 over home-level role files on each OS (obs-plan fct-eodqccd6).

**telemetry-strategy Vector 4 / Founder Direction 4 ↔ log-coverage detail catalog and the wait/last scenario**: socket-dir-refused and server-verify-failed (obs-plan/telemetry-strategy fct-n6l5o3fm, obs-plan/telemetry-strategy fct-4hckhgvs) must read as the same closed detail words on Linux and macOS, macOS an euid mismatch alone with no peer-pid comparison, a CLI wait or last ending at exit 21 during connect and MCP returning instance-unreachable with no line (obs-plan fct-q67chfay).

**telemetry-strategy Metrics / perf-budget-instruments ↔ slo-invariants-telemetry-budgets**: the per-OS perf job on hyperfine --export-json (obs-plan/telemetry-strategy fct-6lxvbxmt, obs-plan/telemetry-strategy fct-olppdytk) must gate the max of the five timed hook rows through gate --require perf, with every hook command run with VIOLA_NAME set and a home under target/e2e-home/ (obs-plan fct-onnnq5uj).

**telemetry-strategy Spans / Traces ↔ ci-integration G1**: the viola-pty seam spans the openpty backend sits behind (obs-plan/telemetry-strategy fct-4joil3ca) must pass G1's bare-instrument gate on all three OSes, only rg exit 1 passing (obs-plan fct-a4sgiwyc).

**telemetry-strategy error-budget-SLO ↔ slo-invariants-telemetry-budgets error budget**: zero panic lines, zero secret-scan hits and zero schema-conformance failures (obs-plan/telemetry-strategy fct-shii35kl) must be measured by in-job gate exit codes on each OS, never the uploaded artifact (obs-plan fct-2v5pxi7x).

body_fields.why: The Unix wrapper's openpty backend must run behind the same manually instrumented pty seam as ConPTY, portable-pty's own log target OFF and its failures captured at the seam, with the child's process-start and process-exit coming from the handle-wait thread on Linux and macOS.
body_fields.quote: none (portable-pty 0.8.1 logs through `log`; its target is OFF and failures are captured at the seam, D-11) | Manual spans on the start sequence, `pty.*` seam, `channel.dispatch`, `run.readiness_gate` (vt100 has no tracing), `run.wheel_transition`, `run.budget_eval`, `state.*`. Child `process-start` / `process-exit` from the handle-wait thread
Every span is manual — no surface has an auto-instrumentation library viola uses, and the rmcp and portable-pty targets are OFF in the sink; channel lines never record `params` or result bodies.
the child's `process-exit` comes from the handle-wait thread, never on reader EOF.

body_fields.why: On the Unix wrapper `pty.spawn` must report `pty_backend` `openpty` from `viola_pty::pty_backend()` and `channel.bind` must report `unix-socket`, never the endpoint name, the pinned path or env values.
body_fields.quote: `channel.bind`: `endpoint_kind` (`named-pipe|unix-socket`);
`pty.spawn`: `pty_backend` (`conpty-sideload|conpty|openpty`, from `viola_pty::pty_backend()`; `conpty-sideload` after a successful pre-load), `env_stripped_count`.
Never the endpoint name, `pinned_bin` path or env values.

body_fields.why: The Unix start sequence must keep the must-trace span chain to `pty.spawn` (with `run.conpty_sideload` Windows-only), keep the Unix-only settings override write span-free, and refuse a socket directory through `socket_dir_ready` with one exit-1 `socket-dir-refused` line before any snapshot, child or bind.
body_fields.quote: **Must-trace spans:** `run.start` (INTERNAL, root) › `state.snapshot_recover` (the start's one snapshot read, `read_snapshot_or_replay`, which the collision check takes) › `run.collision_check` › `run.pin_copy` › `run.conpty_sideload` (Windows) › `run.version_gate` (spawns the `version-probe`) › `channel.bind` › `run.budget_eval` (INTERNAL, `trigger="start"`; its attributes are under Scenario: Budget governor; chunk 2026-10-10-budget-governor) › `state.snapshot_write` › `state.heartbeat_start` › `pty.spawn` (CLIENT).

Two start steps carry no span and no log line, by design (the operator's answer at the chunk 2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through wrap; that chunk's plan added no span name): the statusline source read, whose result is the snapshot's `statusline_command`, and the settings override write (`instances/<name>/settings.json` through `replace_private`, Unix only), which sits between the first snapshot and `pty.spawn`.

A fourth start step carries no span and writes a line only when it refuses: `socket_dir_ready` checks the endpoint's parent, creates it only when absent, then checks again, so a failed create, a lost race and a refused check read one code; a refusal is one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"socket-dir-refused"}`, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`, on `viola revive`'s start too.

body_fields.why: The one diagnostics schema the chunk re-asserts requires `run`'s self and child `process-start` to carry the same fields on Linux and macOS as on Windows, `pty_backend` an open string that admits `openpty`, `sideload_fallback` only on Windows, and the home-tree check to refuse before any log opens.
body_fields.quote: `process-start{subject:"self", service_name, version, os, pid, endpoint_kind}`.
On failure, `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail}` with `detail` ∈ `already-live|stale-heartbeat|squatted-name|pinned-hash-mismatch|batch-script-child|socket-dir-refused`

Before that log opens, the start (`run`'s, and `viola revive`'s) runs the home-tree check `check_home_tree` (through `checked_exe` and `refuse_tree`) on the home (to the read rule), the instance's set, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, `bin/<key>/`, the pinned exe, `plugin/<key>/` and its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`: a refusal exits 1 with the home pair or the instance pair on stderr (`viola revive --json`: its `strict-modes-failed` document), opens no log, writes no line and starts no child, so it carries no `detail`.

On success, `process-start{subject:"claude-child", child_pid, pty_backend, cli_version, cli_verified, env_stripped_count, env_stripped_known, env_kept}` (D-34), plus, on Windows when the `run.conpty_sideload` outcome is not `loaded`, `sideload_fallback` (`hash-mismatch|strict-modes-failed|unreadable|load-failed|not-built`, D-36).

In `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, `pty_backend` is `{ "type": "string" }`, while `sideload_fallback` is closed in the `process-start` properties to `hash-mismatch|strict-modes-failed|unreadable|load-failed|not-built` (`diag-detail.v1.json` carries neither).

body_fields.why: The kill-and-revive case the Unix suite runs (through `tests/support/home.rs`) drives `viola revive`'s start arm, which must log as process `run` only after its instance check passes and write no line on a refused check.
body_fields.quote: `viola revive`'s start arm is not a `cli` verb and logs as process `run` once its instance check has passed (the `viola run` row); a refused check, on either arm, opens no process log and writes no line.

body_fields.why: The hook contract the scope keeps (exit 0, no body, no stderr) must hold under the Unix fake-agent suite: an unresolved or refused instance exits 0 with no line, `catch_unwind` keeps exit 0, and a failed open falls back to a sink.
body_fields.quote: and except a refused or absent instance on the event and dialog paths: the instance check, `canonical` then `trusted`, runs before `read_diagnostics_level` and obs init, and a refused check, or an instance that does not resolve (no valid `VIOLA_NAME`, or a `VIOLA_DIR` naming no existing instance directory), exits 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no role file, no stdin read, no line, no frame and no SessionEnd append). `std::panic::catch_unwind` around dispatch keeps exit 0. The writer falls back to `std::io::sink` on open failure

body_fields.why: On the Unix socket endpoint `channel-request` and `channel-response` must carry the same fields (`corr` and `conn` on both sides, the `-32602` `detail` closed word) as on the Windows pipe, never `params` or result bodies.
body_fields.quote: `channel.request` (client) / `channel.dispatch` (server) spans. `channel-request` / `channel-response` with `method`, `corr`, `conn`, `result_class`, `error_code`, `sender` and, on a `-32602`, `detail` (below). Never `params` or result bodies

on a `-32602` the line carries the closed word of §6, written on both the server's and the client's line by `ResponseLine`'s `Drop` from `ProtocolError::cause` (`None` for the other four faults, so their lines carry none)

body_fields.why: The Unix wrapper's `accept_loop` must drop a peer refused by euid before any frame with no span and no line, the client reading end-of-file, and no test seam may force that refusing decision.
body_fields.quote: No span and no line: `accept_loop` filters each accepted stream by `peer_admitted` over its peer euid, so a refused stream is dropped on the accept thread, before its worker thread and before any frame. The peer reads end-of-file; no frame exists to key a line on; nothing reaches the outer terminal and the wheel does not move

`peer_admitted` refuses a peer of another euid, and a peer it cannot read, where euids are reported (`PEER_EUID_REPORTED`, Unix). On Windows no euid is read, and the DACL and the pid comparison stay the controls.

body_fields.why: The macOS carve-out the scope keeps requires a CLI frame verb's server check to end with exit 21 `server-verify-failed` during connect on all three OSes, comparing pid and start time on Linux and Windows only, so no macOS test reads it as a comparison.
body_fields.quote: A refused euid, a mismatch or a check that cannot be made opens no `channel.request` span, writes no `channel-request` line and ends `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}`. The peer pid and start-time comparison runs on Linux and Windows. `server-verify-failed` reaches Linux, Windows and macOS, where on macOS it means an euid mismatch alone: macOS reports no peer pid, its named carve-out.

A refused euid, a mismatch or a check that cannot be made returns the codes-only `isError` `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed`, no frame and no log line, as the unreachable path does with its own cause. The peer pid and start-time comparison runs on Linux and Windows; `server-verify-failed` reaches Linux, Windows and macOS, where on macOS it means an euid mismatch alone (macOS compares no peer pid, its named carve-out).

a serving process that is not the recorded wrapper (Linux and Windows) or runs under another euid (Linux and macOS) ends a CLI `wait` / `last` before any frame, with one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` at WARN inside the dispatch span and no `channel-request` line, and MCP's returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed` and no line (on macOS an euid mismatch alone, since macOS compares no peer pid, its named carve-out)

body_fields.why: On the hook path the same carve-out holds: a refused euid or failed server check sends no frame and fails open with `hook-decision{detail:"server-verify-failed"}`, pid comparison on Linux and Windows only.
body_fields.quote: A refused euid, a server that is not the recorded wrapper, or a check that cannot be made gets no frame: no `channel.request` opens, and the hook fails open (exit 0, empty streams) with `hook-decision{detail:"server-verify-failed"}`; a SessionEnd whose check fails takes the direct `append_session_end`. The peer pid and start-time comparison runs on Linux and Windows; `server-verify-failed` reaches Linux, Windows and macOS, where on macOS it means an euid mismatch alone (macOS compares no peer pid, its named carve-out).

body_fields.why: These captured-span cases witness the server-check and socket-directory refusals' place that the Unix suite re-reads, and the OS gate on their shared helper must carry its one-OS reason under the scope's cfg rule and the macOS carve-out.
body_fields.quote: The refusal's place is asserted by captured-span cases, one per CLI frame verb (`request_refuses_an_unverified_server_inside_its_dispatch_span` in each verb's module) and one for the hook (`hook_refuses_an_unverified_server_inside_hook_handle`), each through the shared test-only helper `cmd::client::refused_inside` (`assert_refused_inside`): the refusal happens inside its scenario's root span, and each case reads red with the check removed.

The socket-directory refusal's place is asserted by two captured-span cases: `connect_refuses_a_loosened_socket_directory_inside_its_dispatch_span` (`src/cmd/client.rs`), which opens the span by hand (`wait.block`) around `connect`, where the check sits, and `hook_refuses_a_loosened_socket_directory_inside_hook_handle` (`src/cmd/hook.rs`). Their span recorder `Seen` stands in the test module `refused_seen` of `src/cmd/client.rs`, out of the macOS-gated `refused_inside`.

body_fields.why: The frame verbs' instance check must refuse identically on both Unix OSes, the `--json` refusal document carrying the same fields and closed word on every OS, and no line written.
body_fields.quote: the six frame verbs (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`) run `client::refuse_untrusted`, the instance check `link` / `unlink` share, on their named instance before any role file opens; a refused check (exit 21, the instance pair on stderr, or under `--json` exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}`) opens no process log and writes no line.

body_fields.why: `socket-dir-refused` is a Unix-reached closed word the one schema re-asserts: a frame verb writes one exit-21 WARN line inside its dispatch span, a hook one fail-open `hook-decision`, and the human pair stays fixed, ASCII and path-free.
body_fields.quote: a frame verb (`send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`) meeting a refused socket directory writes one `process-exit{exit_code:21, detail:"socket-dir-refused", during:"connect"}` at WARN inside its dispatch span, no `channel-request` line and no frame. The check lives in `cmd::client::connect`, on the recorded endpoint's parent, and changes no mode: a refused directory stays as found.

a hook meeting a refused socket directory writes one `hook-decision{detail:"socket-dir-refused"}` at WARN inside `hook.handle`, on the dialog path after `hook-invoked{corr:null}` and with `decision_emitted:false`; exit 0, empty streams, no frame.
The socket-directory refusal's human pair (design-system §Surface: cli) is printed on start and frame-verb refusals in plain ASCII with `hint:` last and no SGR, and names only the parsed `ViolaName`.

body_fields.why: `mcp`'s lines must stay codes-only and go to the explicit file writer on Linux and macOS as on Windows, the same sink and line schema on every OS.
body_fields.quote: `mcp.tool_call` span per tool (`send · wait · last · answer · list`). Codes-only `send-refused` / `channel-response` on rejects. The writer is always explicit (file; stderr only as a fallback)

body: **span-trace-coverage ↔ log-coverage**: the `pty.spawn` span's `pty_backend` (obs-plan/span-trace-coverage fct-smfiay44) and the child's `process-start{subject:"claude-child"}` (obs-plan/span-trace-coverage fct-4g2at3oh) must read the same `openpty` value on Unix, and the PTY seam's must-log events (spawn's `process-start`, exit from the handle-wait thread, `exit_source:"kill-fallback"`, paste as `text_bytes` only) hold on the openpty backend as on ConPTY (obs-plan fct-3epowryi).

**span-trace-coverage ↔ pii-scrubbing-compliance (G4 schema)**: the Unix `process-start` lines must conform to `schemas/diag-line.v1.json`, where `pty_backend` is an open string and `sideload_fallback` a Windows-only closed field (obs-plan/span-trace-coverage fct-4g2at3oh), under the default-deny `unevaluatedProperties: false` that fails any field outside the catalog (obs-plan fct-llmksgvm).

**span-trace-coverage ↔ error-capture-reporting**: the child's `process-exit` from the handle-wait thread (obs-plan/span-trace-coverage fct-xrkfnxjv) requires the Unix PTY pump and handle-wait threads to run inside `catch_unwind`, no worker panic leaving `main` running without a `process-exit` (obs-plan fct-sue3fxzz).

**span-trace-coverage ↔ log-coverage (detail catalog)**: `server-verify-failed` and `socket-dir-refused` on the CLI, hook and MCP paths (obs-plan/span-trace-coverage fct-2tnvi4o3, fct-kohas2np, fct-ts6ky5ry, fct-zklcva6d) are the closed Unix-reached words; a refused socket directory is never a strict-modes failure and carries its own `detail` (obs-plan fct-wrd7y3z2), with no path or pid inside any `detail` (obs-plan fct-hl4ehpjw).

body_fields.why: The openpty-backed wrapper on Linux and macOS must give the child's process-exit from the handle-wait thread, with exit_source handle-wait or kill-fallback, never on reader EOF, as the Windows wrapper does.
body_fields.quote: The handle-wait thread emits `process-exit{subject:"claude-child", child_exit_status, exit_source:"handle-wait"|"kill-fallback"}`, never on reader EOF (ConPTY chaos class). `run` then emits `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code, duration_ms}`.
the child's `process-exit` comes from the handle-wait thread, never on reader EOF.

body_fields.why: The send's server check must keep the macOS carve-out the scope names: on macOS an euid mismatch alone, no peer pid compared, and no test reading it as a comparison.
body_fields.quote: A server that is not the recorded wrapper, or a check that cannot be made, opens no `channel.request`, and the path ends there (the peer pid and its start time on Linux and Windows; `server-verify-failed` on Linux, Windows and macOS, on macOS an euid mismatch alone, macOS comparing no peer pid, its named carve-out).

body_fields.why: The pty seam's write leg on openpty must carry the same pty.paste_write attributes as on ConPTY: the typed text's length only, never the text.
body_fields.quote: `pty.paste_write`: `text_bytes` (the length of the typed text: the sent text with every CR LF pair and every other CR as one LF, and without its trailing CR and LF characters), `paste_mode="bracketed"`;

body_fields.why: The send's client-side server-verification refusal must write the same closed process-exit on Linux, macOS and Windows, which the one-schema re-assertion reads.
body_fields.quote: client-side server-verification refusal, made after the client's own refusals and before any frame (Linux, Windows and macOS, on macOS an euid mismatch alone): no `channel-request` / `channel-response` line on either side; CLI `send` ends `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` at WARN, and MCP `send` writes no line;

body_fields.why: The exit-21 during words and the send's typed exit set must hold on every OS, the scope adding no exit code.
body_fields.quote: An exit-21 `process-exit`'s `during` is `call` for `endpoint-lost` alone; `instance-dead`, `unwrapped-name`, `server-verify-failed` and `socket-dir-refused` are `during` `connect`.
`send.client` closes with `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code}` (0 / 10 / 11 / 12 / 13 / 14 / 20 / 21, or 1 `internal-error` on a reply with neither a parseable `result` nor an `error.code`)

body_fields.why: wait / last on Linux and macOS must run the socket-directory check, the connect, the euid decision and the server check in this order before any channel.request, macOS comparing no peer pid.
body_fields.quote: The server check runs inside `wait.block` / `last.client`, after the client's own refusals, the socket-directory check, the connect and the euid decision, and before `channel.request`; a refused directory or euid, a server that is not the recorded wrapper, or a check that cannot be made, opens no `channel.request` (the peer pid and its start time on Linux and Windows; `server-verify-failed` on Linux, Windows and macOS, on macOS an euid mismatch alone, macOS comparing no peer pid, its named carve-out).

`wait.block` closes on the response, on the connection error, or on a socket-directory or server-verification refusal made before any frame (no `channel.request` opened; the client's `process-exit` its outcome line).

a serving process that is not the recorded wrapper (Linux and Windows) or runs under another euid (Linux and macOS) ends a CLI `wait` / `last` before any frame, with one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` at WARN inside the dispatch span and no `channel-request` line, and MCP's returns `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed` and no line (on macOS an euid mismatch alone, since macOS compares no peer pid, its named carve-out)

body_fields.why: wait / last exit 21 must carry server-verify-failed or socket-dir-refused with during connect on Linux and macOS, the same closed words as on Windows.
body_fields.quote: `detail:"server-verify-failed"` with `during:"connect"` when the serving process is of another euid or not the recorded wrapper, or the check cannot be made (Linux, Windows and macOS, on macOS an euid mismatch alone), or `detail:"socket-dir-refused"` with `during:"connect"` when the recorded endpoint's socket directory is refused.

body_fields.why: The dialog hook and answer on Linux and macOS must fail open with no frame on a refused directory, euid or server check, macOS comparing no peer pid.
body_fields.quote: A refused directory or euid, a server that is not the recorded wrapper, or a check that cannot be made opens neither: the dialog hook emits no decision (fail open), and `answer` sends no frame (the peer pid and its start time on Linux and Windows; `server-verify-failed` on Linux, Windows and macOS, on macOS an euid mismatch alone, macOS comparing no peer pid, its named carve-out).

body_fields.why: The dialog hook's failed server check must log the same fail-open pair with detail server-verify-failed on every OS.
body_fields.quote: A failed server check is one of those fail-open paths before `dialog_id`: `hook-invoked{corr:null}` then `hook-decision{corr:null, decision_emitted:false, detail:"server-verify-failed"}`, with no `hook.dialog` frame and so no `dialog-raised`.

body_fields.why: pause / release on Linux and macOS must run the socket-directory, euid and server checks before any frame, macOS comparing no peer pid.
body_fields.quote: `pause.client` / `release.client` run the socket-directory check, the connect, the euid decision and then the server check before `channel.request(pause|release)`; a refused directory or euid, a server that is not the recorded wrapper, or a check that cannot be made, opens no `channel.request` and sends no frame (the peer pid and its start time on Linux and Windows; `server-verify-failed` on Linux, Windows and macOS, on macOS an euid mismatch alone, macOS comparing no peer pid, its named carve-out).

body_fields.why: pause / release exit 21 must carry server-verify-failed with during connect on every OS, the same closed words the one schema re-asserts.
body_fields.quote: a server-verification refusal on `pause` / `release`, made before any frame: no `channel-request` / `channel-response` line, the client's `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:21, detail:"server-verify-failed", during:"connect"}` at WARN;

body_fields.why: The statusline-shell pair is a behaviour of Unix alone, so a test reading it must carry that reason where it stands, and a Windows run must write no such pair rather than an OS-only word.
body_fields.quote: `process-start` / `process-exit{subject:"statusline-shell", shell_exit_status, duration_ms}`, only when the snapshot records a `statusline_command` and a shell is built (never on Windows, where `shell_argv` is `None`);

body_fields.why: The openpty child spawn on Linux and macOS must strip CLAUDE names by the Unix rule and log them on process-start claude-child as names only.
body_fields.quote: The strip removes every inherited `CLAUDE*` name (ASCII case-insensitive on Windows, exact on Unix) except the persistent set (Windows `HKCU`/`HKLM` `Environment` value names; Unix `config.json` `claude_env_keep`), and always removes the 11 names of the identity floor `IDENTITY_FLOOR`, measured on the Windows host, whatever the persistent set says
`env_stripped_count`, `env_stripped_known` and `env_kept` on `process-start{subject:"claude-child"}`; names only, never values, and no env map is passed to a span or event.

body_fields.why: The snapshot-replay recovery line must keep the same detail words and fields on every OS, as the task re-asserts.
body_fields.quote: `state-recovered{detail:"snapshot-replayed"|"snapshot-unsupported-v", file:"snapshot.json", v_seen}` (D-03).

body:
Brings Linux and macOS to parity with Windows: on both Unix OSes the `viola run` wrapper runs its child under portable-pty's openpty backend, behind the same pty seam as ConPTY (spawn, read, write, resize, wait, kill).
Runs the full fake-agent suite on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest; a test left cfg(windows), cfg(unix) or cfg(target_os) carries the reason its behaviour belongs to one OS. Adds the Unix integration-tier witness of dim only on stale rows (v1-40).
Re-reads the obs gates G1 to G4 and the CI test, perf and lint jobs, which must be green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest beside windows-2025.
Re-asserts one diagnostics schema on every OS: process-log lines, events.ndjson, snapshots and every --json document carry the same fields and closed words. Where an OS cannot fill a field, it reads its documented null, never an OS-only word.
Windows stays the live-supported target. No live claude session: everything runs on the fake agent.

body: The viola-pty seam on Unix: openpty behind spawn, read, write, resize, wait and kill. It is instrumented at the seam only; the openpty OS API is boundary-only and the PTY byte stream is never logged.

PTY-seam logging on every OS: spawn gives process-start with subject claude-child. The child's process-exit comes from the handle-wait thread, never from reader EOF. Kill-fallback use is logged as exit_source kill-fallback, and paste logs text_bytes only.
The multi-platform exporter-compat trigger: the same file sink and line schema on every OS, with identical fields and no OS-specific exporter or sink.

The required fields on every line (timestamp, level, target, message, event, corr, process, instance) and the additive field catalog. Null is encoded by key absence (the Null encoding rule), and the chunk's documented-null reading of a field one OS cannot fill must act on that rule.

The closed event enum and the closed detail code catalog: no OS-only word, and no path or pid inside a detail code. This includes the Unix-reached details socket-dir-refused, server-verify-failed and strict-modes-failed.

The macOS carve-out: macOS has no peer pid, so server verification there is an euid mismatch alone. A CLI wait or last ends with process-exit exit 21, detail server-verify-failed, during connect; MCP returns instance-unreachable with no line.

Unix channel endpoint telemetry. A peer that accept_loop refuses by euid is dropped before any frame and writes no line; the client reads end-of-file. A refused socket directory gives detail socket-dir-refused before any channel-request line. channel-request and channel-response carry corr and conn on both sides.

run's pre-child refusals on Unix: a socket directory that socket_dir_ready refuses (exit 1, before any snapshot, child or bind), or a home tree another user could write or read, writes exactly the fixed two-line stderr pair through human::refuse. No path or pid, and nothing of run's own on the terminal while the child runs.

The viola revive start arm used by the kill-and-revive case: it logs as process run, makes the home-tree check before that log, and has its own refusals (state files another user could write, no logged session, a missing recorded directory).

The panic hook and catch sites on every OS. There is one single-line event panic record in the home-level role file and none on stderr. The run PTY pump and handle-wait threads each run inside catch_unwind, and every profile keeps panic unwind.
The zero-unlogged-panics invariant and the error budget: zero panic lines as G2 counts them, zero secret-scan hits and zero schema-conformance failures, measured by in-job gate exit codes on each OS.

Gate G1 (bare instrument), G2 (scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh, fail-closed, --probe first, home-level role files only, one exemption for the fake-agent seam's forced panic at src/cmd/hook/seam.rs), G3 (no abort panic strategy) and G4 (both schemas, if always). Each is its own step with shell bash on all three OSes.

G4 schema conformance against schemas/diag-line.v1.json and schemas/diag-detail.v1.json. Both are default-deny through a top-level unevaluatedProperties false, as measured in tests/contract_diag_schema.rs. An unknown event, a missing required field or a field outside the catalog fails the build.

CI step order and conditions in the per-OS test job: tests first, then G2 and G4 if always, with AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1. Harness capture runs on failure. The secret scan (id secret-scan) runs if always. The diag, harness and junit uploads per matrix.os are gated on the scan's success, and the hit report is uploaded on scan failure.

The secret-scan test over every diagnostics file on every OS: Cookie header, CLAUDE values, the content canary, and diagnostics files at 0600 inside 0700 directories (DACL on Windows). It runs before artifact upload.

The per-OS perf job: hyperfine max gates through gate --require perf over the five timed hook rows. Obs overhead on hook holds only when every hook command runs with VIOLA_NAME set and a home under target/e2e-home/.

The lint job on every OS: clippy disallowed-macros, print_stdout, print_stderr and dbg_macro; scripts/lint-probes.sh (raw event outside viola_core obs); and cargo deny (no Tokio in the sync crates, no C-building crates, veil toggle banned).

The liveness signal behind the v1-40 witness: run touches heartbeat every 1 s, and the state flips at more than 5 s (4.9 s live, 5.1 s stale). Short-lived readers read liveness through list --json. No line is logged per tick or per transition.

The hook contract under the Unix suite: exit 0, stdout only the decision body (or the status-line output), stderr empty. A failed log write is swallowed. Without VIOLA_NAME, the hook is a silent no-op with no file opened (E1).
The log file location and modes on every OS: home-level role files run, hook, mcp and cli under diagnostics, and content-bearing detail only in the instance detail file.

Snapshot and --json documents across OSes: absolute paths in snapshot.json and config values are scrubbed from external output, and state-recovered lines (snapshot-replayed, torn-line-healed) keep the same detail words on every OS.
The fake-agent boundary: in CI, viola verify runs only against the fake agent, and the fake-agent seam's deliberate panic is G2's only exemption. Neither may widen to make a Unix case pass.

body_fields.convention: every integration-test viola home lives under target/e2e-home/, so G2, G4, the secret scan and the per-OS diag upload cover it (the one chaos_feed_panic home excepted)

every new log line goes through obs_event! with the closed event enum and catalog-named typed fields only: no raw tracing level macros, no print or eprint, corr passed as a typed value, no path or pid in detail
every new span uses instrument with skip_all first, a static area.operation name and an explicit field allow-list; never err or ret, and never content in span fields

every new CI gate is its own run step with shell bash on all three OSes, if always where it guards diagnostics; uploads come only after the secret scan passes, actions are pinned by commit SHA, and retention is 7 days
every test and fixture input is synthetic, so a detail-file upload stays admissible; no CLAUDE value, Cookie header or real content reaches any diagnostics file
no retry-once policy for panics or flaky telemetry assertions (retries 0), and no log-based wait relying on sleeps; emission keys on hook events and events.ndjson offsets

body: External error reporting: sentry or any reporter, the before_send conditions and the future-reporter Decisions Log precondition. v1 has no reporter, and the chunk adds none.
OTel SDK init, the OTLP exporter, the deferred tracing-opentelemetry bridge, span kinds mapped to otel.kind, and W3C traceparent. None exists in v1, and parity adds none.

The derived metric catalog and its naming (viola area measure, viola.compat.v_rejected) and label cardinality discipline. The chunk derives no new metric; its perf reading is the hyperfine gate named in the Needs.
The not-triggered triggers (compliance-audit-trail, self-observing-inversion) and the obs tier justification in section 1. The chunk changes neither.
Section 1's historical alignment gaps (a) to (c) for Phase 3 (release-from-driver as its own event, the hook-invoked corr timing). Earlier Decisions Log entries settled them, and parity reopens none.

The Windows ConPTY sideload companion: the conpty owner and DACL check, sideload_fallback strict-modes-failed on process-start, and the windows-sys TerminateProcess fallback. These are Windows behaviours the scope holds unmoved.
The dispatch-only windows-mutants.yml workflow (the boundary audit's Windows mutation leg). The chunk neither runs it nor changes it.
Operational retention and the audit-log-retention trigger: no rotation of events.ndjson or diagnostics in v1. The chunk adds no rotation.
Metrics-endpoint and in-process-instrument bans, proprietary APM and dashboards-only bans, and the self-instrumentation ban. The chunk adds no listener, meter, dashboard or collector.
Service identity resolution (service.name viola and version from viola-core constants, never from OTEL env vars). Parity changes no resource attribute.

body: **2026-09-24-three-os-ci-headless-harness-skeleton** — The fake agent (`src/bin/viola-fake-agent.rs`, a root-package bin) is exempted from the print ban by a crate-level `#![allow(clippy::print_stdout, clippy::print_stderr)]`, and only `viola-e2e` carries its own `[lints.clippy]`. Matters because the lint job must read green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest while the full fake-agent suite runs there, with no new `#[allow]`.

**2026-09-24-diagnostics-plane** — Schema default-deny is enforced by a top-level `unevaluatedProperties: false` (not per-event `additionalProperties`), and `diag-detail.v1.json` is self-contained. `obs_event!` attaches `event`, `process` and `instance`, while `corr` is caller-supplied. This is the mechanism by which an OS-only field fails G4 on a Unix leg, which is why a field one OS cannot fill must be absent.

**2026-09-24-log-redaction-and-never-log-floor** — anyhow is scoped to the root-bin dispatch edge and its catch-site reporter `viola::obs::report_internal_error`. The chain goes only to `detail-<process>.ndjson`. The Unix `run` wrapper must keep this error-capture boundary unchanged.

**2026-09-24-observability-gates** — The raw-tracing ban is enforced by the `clippy.toml` `disallowed-macros` path ban plus a fail-closed raw-`event!` grep in `scripts/lint-probes.sh`. That grep runs on the Linux lint leg, and its failure is a build failure (D-33). It bears on the lint job reading green on ubuntu-latest/macos-latest over any new Unix-only code.

**2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows** — `process-start{subject:"claude-child"}` gains `env_kept`. D-34 supersedes D-14: every stripped and kept `CLAUDE*` name is logged, and no value is ever read. `batch-script-child` is decided by program resolution before `pty.spawn`. `PtyError`'s `Display` is hand-written, and the seam spans (`pty.spawn` etc.) are required. The openpty spawn must log the same names-only strip fields, and seam spans must exist on Unix as on ConPTY.

**2026-09-26-ci-chunk-base-and-union-verdict** — The secret scan covers `target/agent-run/*` except exactly `target/agent-run/chunk.diff`, which `harness-<os>` also never uploads. This is the scan scope that must read clean on both Unix OSes before the per-OS uploads.

**2026-09-27-wrapper-channel** — `diag-line.v1.json` makes `corr` required per event (`channel-*`, `dialog-*`, `release-from-driver`, `send-*` wrapper side, some `hook-decision`) and null-by-absence elsewhere (§3 Null encoding). A malformed peer `conn` is logged as `srv_conn`. This is the null encoding P3 must reconcile with the scope's "never a missing key", and these are the channel fields the Unix-socket lines must carry identically.

**2026-09-27-hooks-to-normalised-events** — D-28: the concurrent-append check landed for the hook files: 8 processes, 3 OSes, no line over 4 KiB, with the >4 KiB half deferred to the hook perf gate. It is the precedent for "append atomicity with concurrent hook writers: POSIX `O_APPEND`" yielding identical lines on Unix.

**2026-09-28-hook-perf-gate** (the `perf` job's uploads) — Perf moved from the `test` job into its own per-OS `perf` job with its own G2, G4 and scan. `perf-<os>`/`diag-perf-<os>` are uploaded only on a successful scan, and `secret-scan-perf-<os>` on a failed one. These are the per-OS artifact names and step order the chunk must see green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest.

**2026-09-28-hook-perf-gate** (G2 seam exemption, D-28 over-4 KiB half) — G2 runs as `scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh` (`--probe` first, `test` and `perf` jobs). It exempts only a `panic_location` of exactly `src/cmd/hook/seam.rs:<digits>`, the founder's live ratification of 2026-09-28. The over-4 KiB concurrent append landed on 3 OSes. The exemption must not widen to make a Unix case pass, and the Unix seam panic must render that exact workspace-relative form.

**2026-09-28-cli-output-tokens** — Every `run` pre-spawn start refusal writes two fixed stderr lines through `src/human.rs` `refuse` → `write_refusal` (one `write_all`, no print macro, no `#[allow]`). This is the precedent for any Unix pre-child refusal pair the parity suite reads.

**2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify** (raw backtrace frames; cli internal-error line) — The detail-line `backtrace` is raw frames from `src/panic_frames.rs`: `libc::backtrace` + `dladdr` on Unix and `RtlCaptureStackBackTrace` on Windows, up to 62 strings, never symbolised. Symbolising cost 351 ms and broke the 1.0 s spine bound. The Unix detail line must validate against `diag-detail.v1.json` on both Unix runners, and must not reintroduce symbolisation.

**2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify** (verify's outcome, the uninstrumented capture arm) — `hook --capture` is uninstrumented by design (§10 bounded exemption 5), and verify's outcome is on stdout with a fixed stderr pair on refusal. Both hold under the Unix fake-agent suite and G2's exemptions.

**2026-09-29-verify-stamped-test-homes-and-harness** — `verify-probe` joins the closed `subject` enum (D-35). In CI verify runs only against the fake agent, and the harness `boot` readiness checks the start records. It sets the closed subject set and the fake-agent-only verify that the Unix suite runs.

**2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty** — D-36 sets `pty_backend` to `conpty-sideload|conpty|openpty` from `viola_pty::pty_backend()`. `run.conpty_sideload` is Windows-only, and `sideload_fallback` is present only on a Windows degrade and closed in `diag-line.v1.json`. The openpty wrapper must report `openpty`, and `sideload_fallback` must be absent on Unix, never an OS-only word.

**2026-09-29-t15-07-57-wrap** — The Decisions Log moved to the archive, and its in-force items were lifted into the body. They include the OFF third-party targets (`portable_pty`) with failures captured at the seam (spawn `Err` → `internal-error`, handle-wait `exit_source`, D-11), `pty_backend` as an open string and `sideload_fallback` as closed (D-36), and the R8 strip's 11-name `IDENTITY_FLOOR` (D-34). These are the seam-capture rules the openpty backend must keep.

**2026-10-02-epoch-2b-cleanup** — CI's `AGENT_RUN_KEEP_HOMES=1` keeps every home, so neither harness `cleanup` nor a test home's drop (`remove_owned`) deletes it before G2, G4, the scan and uploads. Without it a green Unix run leaves `target/e2e-home/` empty and G2 fails its non-empty check.

**2026-10-03-mutation-scoring-completion** (§1 kept current) — §1 stays a labelled verbatim copy, kept current. Until a wrap brings a difference current, §3, §6 and §12 win where they differ. This is the section-currency rule the cascade bindings rely on: the re-asserted schema is `diag-line.v1.json` with the §6 catalog, and §10's "no transition logged" beats §1's "on change only".

**2026-10-04-windows-boundary-mutation-workflow** — The dispatch-only `windows-mutants.yml` is the Windows mutation leg, scoring the `cfg(windows)` obs code in `src/panic_frames.rs`. It bears on the extract's `#[cfg(unix)]`-twin pattern and on which leg judges which OS's code.

**2026-10-04-readiness-gate-and-timing-constants** — The vt100 feed thread is a contained worker: `catch_unwind` per feed and resize, one `parse-rejected{vt100-feed}`, `run` continues. The "no worker panic leaves `main` without `process-exit`" ban covers the PTY pump and handle-wait threads. These are the catch sites that must hold under openpty for G2 to read zero on Unix.

**2026-10-04-confirmed-send-with-cl-1-records** (the chaos home outside the scans, F4) — `tests/chaos_feed_panic.rs` witnesses one `parse-rejected{vt100-feed, panicked}` and one `event:"panic"`. Its `TestHome::outside_scan()` home lives outside `target/e2e-home/`, G2, G4 and the scan (founder ruling, live, 2026-10-04), not a second G2 exemption. This is the one home carve-out that must stay unchanged when the suite runs on both Unix OSes.

**2026-10-04-dialog-answers-by-dialog-id** — Perf moved to five hyperfine rows (`pre-tool-use` added on an unstamped session), each required by name by `gate --require perf`. `parse-rejected{ledger-stamps}` gains `strict-modes-failed`, and CI verify runs at 2.1.287. These are the five rows the per-OS perf job must hold on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest.

**2026-10-07-test-homes-off-the-contended-volume** — G2's `find` start points read `target/e2e-home/`, with a trailing slash so a linked scope is descended. On the Linux dev host `target/e2e-home` is a link to an owner-only tmpfs directory. The trap: without the slash, `find` reads an empty scope. No CI runner has the link, so a local Linux G2 and the CI legs walk differently shaped roots.

**2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host** — The R8 strip always removes the 11 `IDENTITY_FLOOR` names measured on Windows. A differing Linux dev-host reading on 2.1.287 stands beside it and moves nothing (home: architecture §Occupied Resources). This is a known per-OS env difference the Unix child spawn's names-only `env_stripped_*` fields must tolerate.

**2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive** — G2's `--probe` other-file case names its planted literal by its home in `scripts/g2-zero-panics.sh`, never as `path:N`. G2 `--probe` must run first on both Unix legs, and a citation sweep must not re-point the planted literal.

**2026-10-09-inner-cr-and-crlf-in-a-sent-text** — `text_bytes` is the typed text's length: every CR LF and other CR becomes one LF, and trailing CR/LF are dropped. The openpty paste must log the same count as ConPTY.

**2026-10-10-windows-mutation-grade** — On the Windows leg the harness leaves `#[cfg(unix)]` twins in `src/panic_frames.rs` out as host-excluded (23 tested, 14 caught, 9 left out). A missed mutant the host never compiles is not counted. This is the precedent for code only one OS builds: Unix-only obs code must be judged on a Unix leg.

**2026-10-10-self-healing-state** — `state-recovered` is written by `read_snapshot_or_replay` (`snapshot-replayed|snapshot-unsupported-v`) and by the healing appender (`torn-line-healed`, `file`, `offset`), one line per call or heal, at WARN with no `corr`. These detail words must read the same on every OS.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** — revive's start arm logs as role `run` into `run-<name>.ndjson`, `human::refuse` gains revive as a caller, and the `process-exit` exit-1 details grow. The kill-and-revive case the Unix suite runs (via `tests/support/home.rs`) drives this arm.

**2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through** — The `statusline-shell` pair is written only when a command is recorded and a shell is built, never on Windows. Two start steps carry no span by design, among them the Unix-only settings override write. These are the Unix-only behaviours a test must name its OS reason for, and Windows writes no OS-only word for them.

**2026-10-10-budget-governor** (a refused instance check writes no line) — revive's instance check moved before log init, and a refusal is the stderr pair with no line. The hook statusline arm's refused check opens no role file, and §10 gains exemption 7. This is the start of the "refused check writes no line" rule, which the Unix suite must read by stderr pair and not as a missing G2/G4 line.

**2026-10-10-budget-governor** (run.budget_eval in the start chain) — `run.budget_eval` was inserted between `channel.bind` and `state.snapshot_write` in the must-trace start chain. This is the chain the Unix wrapper's start must reproduce up to `pty.spawn`.

**2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup** — `process-exit` exit 1 gains `interrupted` for a verify stopped by Unix `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` (Windows Ctrl-C/Ctrl-Break). The handler logs nothing, and the probe dir is left by SIGKILL or a crash. This is a per-OS signal path whose closed word must match across OSes.

**2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows** — A second capture arm, `hook statusline --capture` (Unix only, Run B's probe), is uninstrumented by design (exemption 5). verify's `MM` relied count differs per OS (then 21 Unix / 18 Windows). This is the precedent for a per-OS relied-row count and a Unix-only uninstrumented arm.

**2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows** — A PTY child killed at a Ctrl-C/TERM stop carries `child_exit_status`, because portable-pty reports a code for a signalled child, measured at that chunk. The print-mode/`--version` probe case was not measured. This bears on openpty kill/wait semantics on Unix.

**threat-data ↔ bootstrap logging-redaction-wire and error-handling**: the one diagnostics schema across OSes (security-plan/threat-model-summary fct-qcqqc5fi) (security-plan/threat-model-summary fct-qgluq6ji) must keep the NEVER-log floor (security-plan fct-auxwpgtg) and the closed MCP and CLI --json codes (security-plan fct-kulo4ws7) on every OS, a value one OS cannot fill reading its documented null or closed word.
